These states are the first to act, but not the last. Not when the Supreme Court has rolled back decades of progress and made racial gerrymandering a thing again.
RUSH $35 or more right now to fight back against voter suppression and defend our fundamental right to vote >> [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/ifvap-power?refcode=070726_3&amount=35]
Voter Action Project [https://voteractionproject.org/]
The Supreme Court voted to gut the Voting Rights Act. Now, anti-voting politicians in states throughout the country have a clear path to implement devastating voter suppression schemes, Team.
Opponents of voting rights are already taking new voter suppression actions in Tennessee, Louisiana, and South Carolina , where maps are being hastily redrawn as we speak to gerrymander voting districts, and ballots that were already cast have been thrown out in states like Alabama.
Our tools and programs:
➜ Help voters get re-registered in their new districts.
➜ Find their new polling locations.
➜ Speak up for their right to cast a ballot.
The need for this work is greater than ever before. This is an "all hands on deck" moment , and we are fighting on the front lines to defend the right to vote for every American.

It’s no secret, Peter.

I’ve been on a winning streak throughout my career in public service. 6-0 in statewide races.
I’ve won six tough races here in North Carolina – and whether I was fighting to expand Medicaid, add jobs or increase teacher pay, I put North Carolinians first, no matter what. It has been the opportunity of a lifetime to serve the people and place I love so much.
**You have to know this, though: Having won in the past won’t be enough to win this time around.

** This Senate race is bigger. The stakes are higher. The attacks on and distortions of my record are more outlandish and harmful. The money is pouring in at a rapid pace.
Republican dark-money super PACs are investing nearly $100 million so far to defeat me and keep this seat red – and **it was just reported that my Trump-backed opponent and his allies are outspending us nearly 5:1.**
Peter, I need your help. We’ve been able to stay competitive in this race, but only because of grassroots support from people like you. We have to keep fighting – and we cannot let this Washington DC insider and his MAGA allies buy this seat.
[**_Can I count on you to chip in $5 or whatever you can today to ensure we have the resources to flip North Carolina blue and take back the Senate?_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk778_1&amount=5&t=8&akid=2017%2E124072%2EPWu-aV)

Thank you,

Roy Cooper

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

body:
What I saw at the grocery store this week. | | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134833213/632345707/-903484763?&refcode=E30738-20260708-GroceryStore-Image-Economy&amount=10&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDMxMTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiMGM5NjZhODItNmE3YS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=eB2QuMT0tWRjADIdCDr9TkfzP3VNRkxJecD8U0tJrcc=) Peter, The other day, Pam sent me to the grocery store to grab burgers, hot dogs, and everything we needed for the Fourth of July. _**I couldn't believe the total.**_ More than $5 for ketchup. | | **OPEC Raised Quotas. Hormuz Shipping Is Recovering. The 5-Year Breakeven Rate Hit 2.2%. Three Simultaneous Signals Say July 15 CPI Has a Clear Path Below 3.5%.**
---
| | Three oil and inflation signals arrived this weekend in combination: OPEC and its allies agreed to raise crude production quotas, adding supply pressure to a market already near $68 WTI. Bloomberg reported signs of recovery in Strait of Hormuz shipping, meaning the post-war normalization of tanker traffic is proceeding. And the five-year breakeven inflation rate — the bond market’s real-time measure of expected average inflation over five years — fell to **2.2%** , its lowest level since October 2024, down from 2.7% in mid-May. The Deloitte global economic update attributed the rapid decline to two events: the assumed end of the Iran conflict and Warsh’s public statements on inflation focus. The bond market, in other words, already believes the Fed is winning on inflation. **At 2.2% breakeven, the bond market is pricing a world where July 15 CPI is the beginning of the end of the inflation problem, not a one-off reading.**
---
| | The three signals are mutually reinforcing, and each independently points toward a sub-3.5% June CPI print. ISM Manufacturing prices paid fell from 82.1 to 73.0 in June — the largest single-month decline since 2022, reflecting Brent’s fall from $88 to $74 flowing through manufacturing input costs with its standard 4–6 week lag. OPEC’s production increase means Brent will stay near $68 or lower through July, extending that pipeline into August. Hormuz shipping normalization removes the secondary supply chain cost that had persisted even after crude prices fell. **The remaining risk is Iran succession** — the Assembly of Experts deadline is today, and a destabilizing succession outcome would reverse all three signals. Watch Brent. If it stays below $74 through the succession announcement, the CPI disinflation path is confirmed. If it moves above $76, the three signals are at risk simultaneously.
---

| | **FOMC Minutes Release Wednesday at 2 PM. Without Forward Guidance, This Is Now the Most Important Fed Communication of the Quarter. Three Questions It Must Answer.**
---
| | The FOMC minutes from the June meeting release Wednesday July 8 at 2 PM ET. Under Warsh’s explicitly post-forward-guidance framework — where the dot plot no longer functions as a commitment and pre-meeting signals have been retired — the minutes serve a different function than before. They are now the market’s only structured inside view of what the committee actually thinks. Three questions the minutes must answer: **How close was the vote?** A unanimous hold is very different from a contested 7–5. **How many members wanted to hike in June?** If four or more dissented toward hiking, October becomes near-certain regardless of the +57K payrolls. **How did the committee describe the inflation trajectory?** PCE at 4.1% as a floor means October is locked. PCE as a temporary peak means October is flexible. The answer to those three questions will reprice October hike odds immediately on Wednesday afternoon.
---
| | Wednesday is also approximately the Iran succession deadline — the Assembly of Experts’ five-day constitutional window expires today or tomorrow. **FOMC minutes at 2 PM and Iran succession announcement on the same day creates the highest-volatility session of the week.** The 10-year Treasury yield will move on both simultaneously: dovish minutes push yields lower, hawkish minutes push them higher, while Brent moving above $76 on succession uncertainty adds inflation expectations upward pressure. If the two events move in opposite directions — hawkish minutes pushing yields up while a constructive succession pushes oil down — they partially offset. If they move in the same direction, the session could produce 10+ basis point moves in the 10-year. For the bond investor: hold short duration through Wednesday. For the equity investor: Wednesday is the week’s highest-information session. Do not act before 3 PM when the full picture becomes clear.
---

Bitcoin Was the Prototype
Say what you want about Bitcoin — it proved something the experts swore was impossible.

It proved that millions of people want a way to store wealth that no government can print, freeze, or inflate away. That idea was radical in 2009. Today it's a trillion-dollar fact.

But here's what the true believers don't like to admit: Bitcoin got the idea right and the backing wrong.

It's backed by nothing but belief. It can lose a third of its value in a month. And it consumes as much electricity as a small country just to keep the lights on.

It was the prototype. A brilliant, world-changing prototype — but a prototype all the same.

So here's the question worth sitting with: what happens when someone takes everything Bitcoin got right — the digital freedom, the scarcity, the independence from any government — and fixes the one thing it got wrong, by backing it with real, verified gold?

You get the finished version. And it starts trading on Kraken today (July 8).

And to be clear: this isn't another speculative crypto, and it isn't paper gold. It's backed by real, certified, in-ground gold — the gold stays right where it is, and the value trades.

I'm not going to unpack the whole thing in an email. But I've been watching it closely, it's cleared one of the toughest exchanges in the world, and I put together the full briefing on what it is.

See the finished version →

Get to the good, green grass first...

Brian Hicks, The Prophet of Profit
President & Founder, Angel Publishing

body:
We are forcing seniors to move out of state. Here’s my plan.
Peter,Wisconsin seniors have spent their entire lives working hard, raising families, building our communities, and paying their fair share of taxes.**So why does our state government continue to tax their retirement income?**_Right now, Wisconsin has one of the highest tax burdens on seniors in the region. Because of this, many of our retirees are packing up and moving to states like Florida, Texas, or Tennessee, where their fixed incomes aren't eaten away by state taxes._ When our seniors leave, we lose their wisdom, their volunteer hours, and the family stability they provide to our communities.I want our seniors to stay right here in the state they love._As your Lieutenant Governor, I will fight to eliminate the state taxation of retirement income._**Seniors on fixed incomes shouldn't have to choose between buying groceries, paying for prescription medicine, or keeping their homes because of high state income taxes.** By shrinking the size of our bloated state government, we can easily afford to give our seniors the tax relief they have earned.If you agree that it's time to stop taxing retirement income, please join our campaign today. ### Rural Boundary Town Hall *Virtual*
Zoom + FB Live @SaveSplitOak Friday, July 10th @ 7PM Florida's rural boundary protects the places that make Central Florida special. It helps prevent costly urban sprawl, reduces flooding by preserving natural floodplains, safeguards our drinking water, protects wildlife habitat, and preserves the farms and forests that sustain our communities.
Join us for a virtual Rural Boundary Town Hall on Friday, July 10 at 7:00 PM*to hear from leaders running for office about what they will do at the federal, state, and local levels to protect Florida's natural resources and stop irresponsible development.

### RNC Update: RNC Intervenes to Protect
### Grassroots Canvassing
---

Dear Peter,
The RNC has intervened in a key lawsuit to protect grassroots door-to-door canvassing.
They are defending a bipartisan FEC opinion that allows parties and outside groups to coordinate on voter outreach materials; something the Campaign Legal Center is now trying to block while the FEC lacks a quorum. This is vital work that helps us reach voters and win elections.
Let's keep knocking doors!
Full update from the RNC is below.
Cheers to Victory 2026,
---
| |
---
| |
---
| Janet R. Fogarty MA RNC National Committeewoman MA GOP State Committeewoman
---
| | Brad Wyatt MA RNC National Committeeman

| |
---
| |
---
|
### RNC Intervenes to Protect
### Grassroots Canvassing
---
> Contact: [rncpress@gop.com](mailto:rncpress@gop.com)
> WASHINGTON, D.C. - The Republican National Committee (RNC) today intervened in a lawsuit to protect grassroots door-to-door canvassing.
> "Campaign Legal Center twiddled their thumbs for two years, waiting to sue over an opinion they doesn't like, and now they're trying to win by default because the FEC doesn't have enough commissioners to fight back. The RNC isn't going to let that happen. This advisory opinion lets parties and grassroots groups work together to knock on doors and talk to voters - exactly the kind of engagement our elections should encourage," said RNC Chairman Joe Gruters.
> The RNC filed a motion to intervene in Campaign Legal Center v. FEC, defending a Federal Election Commission (FEC) advisory opinion that allows political parties to collaborate with other organizations on grassroots door-to-door canvassing. Campaign Legal Center (CLC) is suing to strike down the opinion, and the FEC's lack of a quorum leaves it unable to mount a defense.
> Background:
> In March 2024, the FEC confirmed that political parties may coordinate with outside organizations on canvassing literature and scripts without triggering federal contribution limits. The bipartisan opinion passed 4-2. Campaigns, parties, and outside groups across the political spectrum have relied on it ever since.
> Campaign Legal Center filed suit on May 6, 2026, seeking to vacate the opinion. But the FEC now has only two sitting commissioners -- two short of the four votes required to authorize a legal defense.
> The RNC's motion argues it is entitled to intervene. The FEC's consent to the RNC's participation in the case, combined with its inability to mount a defense of its own, underscores why the RNC's intervention is necessary.
> ###
>

## States Seek $1.4 Trillion from Meta
Four states are seeking a whopping [$1.4 trillion in penalties](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unTAQhJ8GOiP_AKZxkYbupk2JFryGTYx9ZO-5hLePSJQnuO3o06eZ-fGxfABFSvt3ONFxyEvCq0ZkxrKcyFDf6EMuqudCMVJOF8Rz0VKPQlohp8UDxXvpW-8CokbTolN2MoMcRjO0h1u33oceV2vtaL3xBtVogwE1GKuDCS25xyatnJRUZjDdqsDjNmg5aUCQa9NL9MS5dD8zJT4wxDt_Yum2fLbRHcyv2phvjZ4bPV_X1YX8e31XSljrwzR6ZtyOlGPe70bPIb-LqAyMVVTEX5R2oUQv_i8UL0wQmbCK7aDoRc0bQRQnegIB3tPGD8blX8ogKty1Lc6_rkdRR9v0cj-B4t-O_KVjP53-EwAA__-axZEM) from Meta, claiming Facebook and Instagram were designed to addict children and that the company misled the public about the platforms' safety. The sum approaches Meta's [entire market capitalization](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykUD2PpDAU-zXQgZJHSLgixTV0c-2V6EEeQ27yMUreDZp_v2JX-wu2s2zLsv33ttzQB5_ufzCS5T0vic4aiJnKEomx_ie35yIVFx-Cz-nEEBcQoDthOjEtDn14L6p1dicCGlqy0kzDKEY9jO1hFQiHk1FITq1unwy4VUqnf0llVmnW1tsrTRgxSSGHcehXiY62EcQESCjWRglynnPp_2Wf-KA9vPOLSr_l2AZ7MD9rM_xuYG5g3n3CtFH_xiPny9HAHLE8iGsDc-W8PS6Ahf0W6ItDptqdmLiTneq-h3YSlBGgte4PjqEt1j3PS6raNErcI_rwWYF_9NvLwkcAAAD__wNYgaQ) of roughly $1.5 trillion. California, Colorado, Kentucky, and New Jersey calculated the figure by multiplying estimated young users harmed by fine amounts set under state law. Meta called the amount unsupported by the facts and far in excess of any previous consumer-protection fine. The trial is set for next month in Oakland, California.
## Walmart Slashes Summer Prices
Walmart announced it was [cutting prices on thousands of groceries](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGOpDAQBNCvgczI2HjgAgeXTDaXXojadjN4ZWPW3Qw7f79if2HjKpVK7_9jfkBMcXv-g4yWlzJveFJCZqxzRgY6MCyl9gPXmFIs2wkpz0qqm5CjkNMcIKb3PLTBLogKdYu2HydtpLlp067Wg1sADLpej8Ybr72cFue81uqPG4e-jfZak6OcetlrozvXQ0BvlJwUIEjXDBJD5FK7jxI3XnFJ7_LC2vmS22RX5p0a_bdR90bdz_PslvLlDoobEl2dRt0rMsR0xZAyVBYEmYRPhxOUgFax1-iRBK_lINgCib2WcHgmwfXIuyB4k8jlhcJDRrFGEhU_DyRuqw37ednQbWwG-cwQ0881_pXny6rvAAAA__9wP47r) and household items at both Walmart and Sam's Club, with discounts on beef, soda, produce, and seasonal goods to help consumers struggling with high prices. President Trump praised Walmart for the move, saying the cuts came at his administration's request. Walmart declined to comment on Mr. Trump's post. Among the steepest drops: [24-packs of Coca-Cola fell 33%](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkL2OqzAQhZ8GOiP_Ailc3CZdbrslGuxx4l2DkT0JytuvnFfYbqRPc46-83VbbhBT3O__YUNLIS87njUhEZZlQ4L6RB9yEZpKTCnm_YS0LZLLkfGJ8XnxENN70b23AVGi6tGKaVaGm1GZ_mGNgnHGMOtw0UKJ0auLHgU3TgUEhaaPtqXxic-CC2XUsArw6IzkswQEvnaao4-Uy_Cd404PDOmdX1gGl7c-2QfRUTv1r5PXTl7P8xzcWptF4528trMBSBsUYkeJDpl7UmUrYmAu_yA78KiRuVx29qEFob32xfrjbN51nDrN7xvE9KmlP231svI3AAD__yTrfoA) to $9.97, ground beef dropped 12%, and fresh corn plunged 63% to $0.25 an ear. The cuts come as inflation has hit its highest level in more than three years.
## List: Which States Tip the Most
America's average restaurant tip has [slipped to 18.8 percent](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOiNjsDGFizTXXdqUaMHLsZGxkb136P4-IvmE1PM0o3lf9-kOFCg-PmFHx2uaIp4lIDPmaUeG8kS_ptz2nCkESvGEsE9KKiPkIKSdPFB4T33t3YqosKvRtYPttNSm0_XmFgXWaxjHftSzGUG2q7FmtvOA1vTzWJO72uQgbSvbTnfN3ILHRStpFSDIueoleuKUm-9EkTdcwzu9MDdL2uvgNuajVN1HpW6Vup3n2byoPCEscBBDoMIXeEUbZhSwY6YFYhGFKQTBdAglBUQv_gDe8C18ilypW52dP87reDFD1cvHDhR-d_lfsl5O_QQAAP__O0x_jg), an indication that the long-standing 20% benchmark is no longer the norm, according to a 2026 state-by-state report. At the state level, Delaware customers tipped the most, at an average of 22.1%, and California the least at 17.3%. Overall, full-service restaurants receive much larger gratuities than quick-service restaurants, averaging 19.3% versus 15.8%. The growing use of digital payment screens has expanded tipping requests well beyond traditional restaurants, prompting debate over when gratuities are appropriate. You can see [where your state ranks here](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLFuhDAQRL8GOiNjsDGFizTXXdqUaMHLsZGxkb136P4-IvmE1PM0o3lf9-kOFCg-PmFHx2uaIp4lIDPmaUeG8kS_ptz2nCkESvGEsE9KKiPkIKSdPFB4T33t3YqosKvRtYPttNSm0_XmFgXWaxjHftSzGUG2q7FmtvOA1vTzWJO72uQgbSvbTnfN3ILHRStpFSDIueoleuKUm-9EkTdcwzu9MDdL2uvgNuajVN1HpW6Vup3n2byoPCEscBBDoMIXeEUbZhSwY6YFYhGFKQTBdAglBUQv_gDe8C18ilypW52dP87reDFD1cvHDhR-d_lfsl5O_QQAAP__O0x_jg).

|
Peter,
A new blatantly illegal scheme by Trump to rig the upcoming midterm elections just dropped. And this one has the potential to be deadly if states don't comply.
FEMA is now threatening to withhold federal grants for terrorism prevention to states that don't comply with a list of election related demands. They are demanding states switch to paper ballots, use the federal "SAVE" database to purge voter rolls, and to conduct background checks of all election related workers to verify citizenship status.
---
| [](https://yfq78zhbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001G8WOZrTluXnhNr8agS64q7FOOQqSUw6gFLpq-J8q_nXd-gszd5hWSjrExJ3NEuHpuQJC-b7LeYBfKr2hiPtadtQ5DePS7ojk76Ebt1RQ2JJWgpGQ3SQAMEGKcynC-bPH18ZGhKRPw6Bgenyv4VK8xE1StwUf-XePRUhF1e89r40UpTPDkezYbVp5As4yzmOmJkV2uSbH4JTJY5ZoQCxaIZEaw1HQlPKY&c=gxVFfQ_CX5tr-7TswZsPoiZTULKJVFjUgCRB6MAdZO4_0koczJJCoQ==&ch=Z5WEiZz6yfOatH5KcXzWtEpOYBsW6iug0CpypJfoxvlRTeWKp4GVew==)
---
The requirement to use the federal "SAVE" database to purge voter rolls is particularly illegal. Just weeks ago, a federal judge ordered the Trump administration to immediately end and delete the database, citing a "major violation" of American's privacy rights. It was also revealed in that court case that the database was wrongfully purging Democratic voters from the voter rolls.
Trump has significantly ramped up his election rigging attempts in recent weeks. FBI raids against voter rights organizations, USPS threatening to not deliver mail-in ballots in blue states, a renewed push to get the Senate to pass the most restrictive voting law in American history.
He's desperately throwing everything he has at the wall in hopes that something will stick--and that he can get the right judge to greenlight it.
That's why Defend Our Courts is leading a multifront counterassault against Trump's election rigging schemes. First, we are building a firewall of state Supreme Courts with the power to protect free and fair elections, state by state. Second, we are building the movement to reclaim a United States Supreme Court that has made itself an arm of the Trump administration.

## Toyota Moves Tacoma Production to Texas
Toyota is bringing the Tacoma back to Texas. The automaker [announced Monday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLESmzAMhp_GbOZkQ7AZPHRhS9eOnMBKcGtsDishefse9BG66HT6T_r1f7_u4x1DDOn5E1dy_HnkMdFRIjHTPnL-ZsY1v0N6Ms55Rc5MHyyjBt1JMBLs6DHE79hW3k3ge1WRU8Y2N7AdQLU4NF4bO88tmq5toJ-stR6NuvlWK5qgCu48BgasUtCovlZdN5ke2tkqQH0j0QL5wHmveaHL_hG_-U17Pee1im5h3opofgg9CD0cx1H_KcinKPRwphF6iHnGKPRwWgk9gDlLdw0AZKJD_s5TkesrcpBTiDHkJOmzYSpnt0VMibx85F2W_OJFluBJ_uNzqSz0UO3Ob8e5XDojWniuGOL1JP8f2rfTfwMAAP__ft6NXA) a $3.6 billion expansion of its San Antonio plant, adding a second assembly line and roughly 2,000 jobs by 2030 as it shifts most Tacoma pickup production from its [Tijuana, Mexico, facility](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGOgzAMhp8mbEFOoIEOGW5h6603opCYNrokRuCW9u1PtI9wmyXLn__v_7mMFxdTLNdvl9Hyc6ax4L4lZMZ1ZHoRu0yPWK7sPGXHxPh026hBGwmdhH4MLqbX2FbBThDOqkKrur45QW8AqpttGj8FP83OnwBRB9OrOXg1-8mEWfVYRXvAoINeKWjUuVbGTN0ZWt8rcPqEogUMkWmt-Ybv93N60QPX2lOukr0xL5tovoQehB72fa_9tB0Wx17o4RiFHj4yspFGTjGlSEW-YXJJrrDcXJGuMJVI8uMql-h_74tcVgp3z8fBvFKWGZ_Rk9BDtdqw7AdrM51o4ZpdTO9Q_L8qH1b_BQAA__8eqozp) to the Alamo City over the next four years. The project adds 2.5 million square feet, doubling the South Side campus, already home to the Tundra and Sequoia, and bringing [Toyota's total investment](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2unDAQhZ8GOq_GBmwoXKShu2lTogEPixX_IDwX2LePdu8jpB2Nzvm-8-dr-kIffHr-xkiW7zVPia4SiJmOifMrM8Z8-vRkXHJEzkw3lkmB0gKMgH5y6MNramtnZ3CDrMlK0zcd9Bqg3mzfOeqMI1qlmWekGUEjrf2gFZhFYe3tOwwM9FJCI4eH1Ho2A7RLLwFVR1UL5Dzn48EbferX8MonHY8lxzrYjXkvVfOrUmOlxuu6Hmu-5-_iE5Xy_qnUGPH4S1wqNf44CZ9OKiwaoWexB0ws6N4xFZ-TKJtfWfwIi_3I7nvh9309chSRbr9k8eGoD-v2y4fgizZVC8-IPnyo-P-2PK36FwAA__-xYY3W) there to $8.3 billion since 2003. body:
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1135?t=1&akid=857%2E3892029%2EQnisOT)

Peter,
I made an extremely difficult decision six years ago today.
After months of bullying, intimidation, and retaliation from the White House, I submitted my resignation from the U.S. Army.
This wasn’t an easy call. I dedicated 21 years to serving our nation — under presidents of both parties — and put my life on the line to defend our Constitution. I had no plans to retire.
That is, until President Trump made me his #1 enemy.
Months earlier, I witnessed Donald Trump’s so-called “perfect phone call” with Ukrainian President Zelenskyy. As I sat in the Situation Room, I witnessed Trump demand Ukraine do him a “favor” and find damning information on President Joe Biden.
My heart sank. With the 2020 election right around the corner, Donald Trump invited a foreign government to dig up “whatever you can” to investigate an American citizen and smear a political rival for his own benefit.
**This was corruption at its worst. So after reporting the phone call to the proper authorities in the White House, I testified in front of the House of Representatives.**
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260708-1&refcode2=857_3892029_QnisOT&akid=857%2E3892029%2EQnisOT)
That decision changed my life forever. It led to the president’s first impeachment — and subsequently his retribution campaign against me and my family. After months of relentless attacks, I was forced to retire and end my 21-year Army career.
I knew the risk I was taking by standing up to Trump. But as someone who served for decades in the U.S. Army, I fell back on my oath to defend our Constitution and protect our country. _I refuse to let anybody — including Donald Trump and his minions — stand in the way of that oath._
**The fight to defend our democracy isn’t over, which is why I recently made another decision: I am running for the United States Senate in Florida.** The latest polls show that we can flip this seat blue and protect our democracy in the Senate...but I cannot do it alone.
**So, I am asking:[Will you donate $3 to my campaign for Senate today? We need to raise another $70,000 before midnight to stay on track with our July fundraising goal.](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260708-1&amount=3&refcode2=857_3892029_QnisOT&akid=857%2E3892029%2EQnisOT)**

# **Report: Nearly half of NYC public school students attend failing schools**
A sweeping **[analysis by Success Academy Charter Schools](https://substack.com/redirect/9cdf53ab-1e50-48c5-bd09-31e3e1f0564c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** found that 906 New York City public schools, attended by roughly 43% of the system's 912,000 students, failed to have a majority of students pass math, reading, or both on state exams last year. The report, titled "By Any Honest Measure," found some schools have appeared on state accountability lists for decades, with failure becoming normalized rather than addressed.
* **The report accuses city and state policymakers of actively obscuring the crisis** through grade inflation, lowered standardized test benchmarks, and policies that exclude test performance from student grades and bar test scores from teacher evaluations. The result: 98% of teachers receive satisfactory ratings while nearly half of students are failing.
* **New York spends $36,293 per pupil annually -- double the national average** -- yet pumps even more funding into the worst-performing schools despite plummeting enrollment, while blocking expansion of higher-performing charter schools through legislative caps.

* * *
# **Sunny Hostin doubles down on claim that American flags make her feel unsafe**
"The View" co-host Sunny Hostin revisited an eyebrow-raising 2021 statement during a discussion of America's 250th anniversary, reiterating that she feels uncomfortable entering neighborhoods heavily displaying American flags. Hostin claimed that a segment of the country has weaponized the flag to signal White supremacy, making it feel threatening rather than patriotic to some Black Americans.

* **Hostin 's remarks came after the panel discussed a viral photo of uniformed White nationalists on a Washington DC Metro train.** Guest host Michelle Buteau extended the critique beyond fringe groups, questioning why exactly America's 250 years were worth celebrating given supposed ongoing racial inequities.

| | | Meg Caldwell didn’t have to die.

She was a bright young woman from Florida. A talented horse rider, the youngest of four sisters. Her family says she was “the light of our lives.”

Sadly, she passed away this year, overdosing on nitrous oxide.

Yet another life lost to drugs. One of more than _200 a day_ in America this year alone.

But what if I told you that Meg’s death, and the epidemic of addiction sweeping the country... has the same root cause as:

* The explosion of pornography and prostitution
* The rise in violent crime and homicide
* The millions of young men addicted to gambling
* And the moral collapse of everyday American life

Because it _does_.

name: Caitlin Cattelino
subject: Policy Updates: Wildlife Wins and What's Coming Up!
body:
Celebrate some wins for wildlife and learn more about what issues Defenders is tracking through the end of the year!

Celebrate some wins for wildlife and learn more about what issues Defenders is tracking through the end of the year!
                  

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5730402/38SyG9Xl)

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5730402/38SyG9Xl)

Dear Defender,

We have reached the halfway point of 2026! Let’s look back at some successes from the beginning of the year and look ahead to other priority issues we are tracking.

A Win for Wildlife: Anti-ESA Bill Defeated

You likely heard about the big win for the Endangered Species Act on Earth Day. Representative Bruce Westerman’s (R-AR) highly destructive bill, the ESA Amendments Act of 2025 (H.R. 1897), aka The Extinction Act, was pulled off the House floor before a vote was held – due to concerns from House Republicans! The headline from The New York Times article covering the expected vote summed up the success best – “Republicans Had an Earth Day Plan to Limit Species Protection. It Flopped.” (Read it here without a paywall. (https://support.defenders.org/s/5730403/38SyG9Xl))

What you may not have heard is that some of Defenders’ advocates had a front-row seat for the defeat of H.R. 1897 while they were in Washington, D.C. participating in our annual fly-in. To celebrate Earth Day and to raise awareness and support for the ESA, Defenders brought 20 advocates from six different states to Capitol Hill to urge their Members of Congress to VOTE NO on H.R. 1897. They teamed up with other advocates and conservation professionals to deliver critical messages of support for endangered wildlife to crucial swing representatives. As The New York Times article described, key republican representatives, including some in Florida, expressed their doubt to House Leadership regarding Rep. Westerman’s bill to eviscerate the ESA. As support for the bill began to crumble, House Leadership suddenly cancelled the vote.

I was eating lunch with four Coloradans in the Senate cafeteria when I received the news that the bill was pulled from the House floor. We celebrated together with high fives and hugs, knowing that our advocacy and stories of support for endangered species played a vital role in defeating H.R. 1897.

(https://support.defenders.org/s/5730404/38SyG9Xl)

A Win for Wildlife – Protecting Arctic Wildlife from Drilling

In early June, the Bureau of Land Management held an oil and gas lease sale on the Coastal Plain of the Arctic National Wildlife Refuge (https://support.defenders.org/s/5730405/38SyG9Xl). This was the third lease sale in the Arctic Refuge – and the third failure. Of the 58 tracts offered for lease, only five received bids. Nine total bids were submitted by two oil and gas companies. (Here’s our press release (https://support.defenders.org/s/5730406/38SyG9Xl) from the lease sale.)

Additionally, public pressure made a difference. Thousands of people – including 10,000 Defenders’ members and supporters – spoke out, urging oil and gas companies directly to stay out of the Arctic Refuge. And they heard us! No major oil and gas companies bid on any leases!

Despite the lease sale flop, the fight to protect the Arctic Refuge is far from over. We must continue to tell Congress and oil and gas executives that drilling on the Coastal Plain is bad for the planet and for wildlife. And, we must fight to ensure leaseholders do not move forward with development!

What’s Next?

Since the start of the 119th Congress in January 2025, over 80 pieces of legislation (https://support.defenders.org/s/5730407/38SyG9Xl) undermining the ESA have been introduced. In the second half of 2026, we’ll be keeping our eyes open for additional attacks on endangered wildlife and the habitats they need to survive, as well as the critical conservation laws established to protect our wildlife and our public lands. Will we see Rep. Westerman try to push through H.R. 1897 in the “lame duck” period after the November elections? It’s hard to say, but one thing is for certain – we will be watching closely and ready to defeat it again!

In addition to monitoring standalone anti-wildlife bills, we'll continue to track must-pass legislation like the Interior Appropriations bill and the National Defense Authorization Act. Often times, Members of Congress will try to include anti-wildlife language that won’t pass on its own in must-pass bills as riders or amendments. In May 2026, the House version of the FY27 Interior Appropriations bill (https://support.defenders.org/s/5730408/38SyG9Xl) was introduced and included 20 poison-pill riders attacking wildlife including the gray wolf, grizzly bear and wolverine. We anxiously await the Senate’s version of the Interior Appropriations bill and hope that, as in the past, it is clear of any new policy riders attacking wildlife and public lands.

Your voice will continue to be critical in the fight to protect the wildlife we cherish and the cornerstone environmental laws established to protect them and the habitats they need to survive and thrive. Defenders will keep you updated on ways you can help and speak up for the wildlife who are most in need of our help.

Thank you for all that you do,

Caitlin Cattelino

Director of National Outreach

Defenders of Wildlife

(http://www.facebook.com/DefendersofWildlife) (http://twitter.com/defenders) (https://www.instagram.com/defendersofwildlife/?hl=en) (http://www.youtube.com/defendersofwildlife) (https://www.tiktok.com/@defendersofwildlife)

Defenders of Wildlife 1130 17th Street NW • Washington, DC 20036 defenders.org (https://defenders.org)

Control of the Senate is on the line
# [](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/188?t=1&akid=2480%2E135344%2EDAj2Wc)

**Michigan.**
It is, was, and has always been Michigan.
Control of the Senate will run through this state, and given the events of this week I am hoping that you will step up and make a contribution to the Michigan Senate Democratic Nominee fund -- money that will be available on DAY ONE for whoever wins the nomination.
Earlier this week, Mallory McMorrow dropped out of this race. She ran a campaign rooted in her vision for the future. I appreciate her hard fought run, and I look forward to working with her in the future.
That leaves two candidates, both of whom will spend every last dollar they have in order to win the primary while Mike Rogers stashes away his cash to hammer them with attacks the moment they become the nominee.
A contribution to the Michigan Senate Democratic Nominee funds ensures the eventual nominee will have the resources to combat those attacks.
Maybe you have a preferred candidate in the Democratic primary, but this donation I am asking you to make is about keeping this seat BLUE, which is something I know we all agree on.
[**If keeping Michigan's Senate seat blue and helping Democrats take back control of the Senate is important to you, please split a contribution between the Michigan Senate Democratic Nominee fund and my work to help keep this seat blue.**](https://act.elissaslotkin.org/go/9?c0=ebs-em-misen-split.JISqyu&refcode=em250812-1&t=2&akid=2480%2E135344%2EDAj2Wc)

### But Democrats should be alarmed by candidates winning primaries on unworkable, unpopular platforms.
| | [Ben Samuels](https://substack.com/@bensamuels)
---
| Jul 8
---

If you pay way too much attention to politics, as I do,1 there's been a lot of coverage about how progressives--and members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) specifically, who are to the left of progressives--have won a bunch of recent U.S. House primaries.
It is true that DSA members unseated incumbents [in New York City](https://substack.com/redirect/f9b92a30-cbbf-46aa-bf9c-c349cb25e917?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and [in Denver](https://substack.com/redirect/766e2d67-46e6-4dcf-a7cf-79b0e4abb501?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). A few other things are true:
1. The DSA is [remarkably unpopular](https://substack.com/redirect/ffdb71c1-d62a-47ca-873b-71d06b3be1b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) among the general public, and moving to the left to placate a loud but small part of the base is a sure-fire way to lose some otherwise winnable general elections.
2. Even if DSA members win every competitive primary they're in for the rest of this cycle, they'd represent under 5% of the Democratic U.S. House caucus.
3. The media has done a terrible job covering trends in Democratic primaries, selectively extrapolating from a few elections in NYC.
4. Moderate Democrats are right to be worried about the direction of the party.

**Being moderate isn 't inconsistent with being ambitious**. Moderate Democrats _should_ be pushing for more ambitious reforms; but to do that, you need to run on policies that are popular enough to get you elected, and popular enough to garner support from Republicans.
[Subscribed](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly9iZW5zYW11ZWxzLnN1YnN0YWNrLmNvbS9hY2NvdW50IiwicCI6MjA0NDM4NDkyLCJzIjoyNDQwMzk4LCJmIjp0cnVlLCJ1Ijo5MDUwMTE5MiwiaWF0IjoxNzgzNTE1NTMyLCJleHAiOjIwOTkwOTE1MzIsImlzcyI6InB1Yi0wIiwic3ViIjoibGluay1yZWRpcmVjdCJ9.vL_PCNgIZDoPgkU4ZSlFGduqbz1VBNqavD6QumHXCUg?)
### No, the DSA isn't taking over
This was _The Wall Street Journal_ opinion page late last week, with stories about socialism highlighted in red.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ec793a21-4aec-4fa8-8158-48a58a54a988?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
From the afternoon of July 2.
It _is_ true that no matter how the primaries play out over the next couple of months, the ranks of Democratic Socialists in the U.S. House will increase by multiples.
But those multiples are off of a very, very small base.
Right now, there are [two members of the U.S. House](https://substack.com/redirect/ed3e4e90-d4fc-4dff-bda0-3a870f30927b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) who are DSA members. That will increase to at least six2 in the next election; it may increase a bit more than that.
Let's assume that the DSA, somehow, gets to 10 members of the U.S. House next session.3 Even in that scenario, which isn't particularly likely, DSA members will still make up less than 5% of the Democratic caucus,4 and 2.3% of the House as a whole.
There are 435 members of the U.S. House; in any given year, there's no shortage of lunatics. A few more of them are adding a DSA label onto their lunacy, but that doesn't make it a takeover worthy of wall-to-wall _WSJ_ coverage.
### The media's coverage of the DSA wins has been abysmal
That the DSA is growing its ranks is, absolutely, a story.
But based on the day-after coverage, you'd think it was a seismic change in the composition of the party. That's certainly how everyone in the press covered it: _[The Wall Street Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/cd58057c-aaf9-4fcd-ad06-17b2917cb53c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , _[The Washington Post](https://substack.com/redirect/65817675-9c30-4e3f-9f0c-895bfe2db874?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , _[The New York Times](https://substack.com/redirect/2f5625fc-a514-40ef-a154-0bedca833b52?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , _[Politico](https://substack.com/redirect/27d57e23-2b76-4d11-892d-aa5c10b74fa1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , _[Reuters](https://substack.com/redirect/6c59e74d-81b8-4d6b-a93a-597953fd8164?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , [the Associated Press](https://substack.com/redirect/c63c5659-0397-4796-9d5e-e769e033754e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/81bc37e7-13ee-4b11-9beb-9ef2dadc36d2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [NPR](https://substack.com/redirect/089daad5-c26f-4535-a892-48b415a9a2fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [the BBC](https://substack.com/redirect/5759b1a6-9d2b-405c-a194-5e1e5898d1fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), _[The Guardian](https://substack.com/redirect/9e5aedd3-2e4c-4a53-892d-b7bda6efe819?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ , the list goes on.
Part of this is that way too many reporters live in New York City, and as a result, NYC politics is chronically overcovered.5
Because the races below got a fraction of the media coverage, you may be unaware that on the very same night as the NYC primaries:
1. [Adrian Boafo](https://substack.com/redirect/9ab56d98-fb13-4858-a7dc-dab9a35ab823?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), the 32-year-old Maryland delegate,6 [won his congressional primary](https://substack.com/redirect/9ab56d98-fb13-4858-a7dc-dab9a35ab823?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) against far more progressive candidates. He's now running in a safe Democratic seat and will almost certainly win in November.
2. [Ben McAdams](https://substack.com/redirect/a748b75a-8fe9-4357-ab3a-940fb2b2c209?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), a former member of the centrist Blue Dogs in the U.S. House, handily won a primary for a safe Democratic seat against Bernie Sanders-endorsed state senator [Nate Blouin](https://substack.com/redirect/c73b522a-f2aa-4979-b553-ed398a082df4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
3. Most importantly, less than an hour up the road from NYC,7 moderate [Cait Conley](https://substack.com/redirect/2416e0d6-9203-4e85-b975-db0c1da238b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) won [her primary against an Our Revolution-endorsed opponent](https://substack.com/redirect/974f2612-6628-4c96-b229-56a1150c2f5a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in a swing seat held by Mike Lawler, a Republican.8

Why is this most important? Because if you care about Democrats actually winning back the House, then Democrats should nominate moderate candidates. DSA-aligned candidates do terribly in general elections.

### DSA nominees do really poorly in general elections
All of the elections I've written about above are primaries, not general elections. That's notable because the [DSA is immensely unpopular among American voters](https://substack.com/redirect/ffdb71c1-d62a-47ca-873b-71d06b3be1b5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Here's how candidates endorsed by Justice Democrats and Our Revolution, groups in the same ideological lane as the DSA, perform in general elections.9
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/11fba35a-f6df-45fd-8e00-17a8e8472257?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
For all that people talk about the polarization of politics, **candidate quality still matters, and people are less likely to vote for candidates they see as extreme**.10 That won't matter in the races with DSA nominees because they're all in extremely Democratic seats--even underperforming candidates won't cost Democrats those elections.11
But there are [vanishingly few competitive U.S. House races](https://substack.com/redirect/7745c428-da66-43b5-aebf-7d625c3b29da?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--[only 9% of U.S. House races](https://substack.com/redirect/fb89ba69-55e7-4b26-936b-4b14b1a413e0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) are competitive12--and if Democrats want to win back the House, the political alignment of candidates matters a great deal.
To date, Democrats have done a decent job of this, nominating more electable House candidates in [Nebraska](https://substack.com/redirect/6fca84b2-5c96-43f8-ae00-3b53208bf204?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [Texas](https://substack.com/redirect/01bc0fbc-f992-4f03-9869-c7d7cc594372?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg),13 and a few seats in [Pennsylvania](https://substack.com/redirect/c779489f-175a-4e50-9173-35e212da353b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That hasn't been universally true--Democrats nominated a weaker candidate in a [competitive Colorado U.S. House race](https://substack.com/redirect/dcf7511b-dbb8-46b7-b2b1-50d1afcba8a5?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--but the consistent media narrative isn't exactly backed by what's been happening outside of New York City.
There are still primaries to go--Cori Bush is running against Wesley Bell in Missouri-01 again,14 and the Democrats may very well nominate a [particularly bad candidate for the Senate in Michigan](https://substack.com/redirect/ad07bfd4-6f90-4209-a969-ab08139533a1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).15
[](https://substack.com/redirect/bf234e96-8eed-422d-9ca1-c15c1e08f69e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)| | |

But no, the DSA hasn't taken over the Democratic Party. With that said: if the party fails to distance itself from DSA impulses, it will cost Democrats at the ballot box, something [we saw play out already](https://substack.com/redirect/cc54aa93-1728-47ed-b476-da003c621deb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in 2020.16
### What should we learn from recent primaries?
Let me say three things here:
1. I don't believe there is an equivalency between DSA leadership and MAGA leadership. I strenuously object to a lot of what the DSA says, does, and believes. But I don't believe that there's the same anti-democracy instinct, willingness to subvert laws, or [self-dealing](https://substack.com/redirect/130fd3f3-4a99-4326-ba19-d368020d4d4f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that's evidently a Trump administration prerequisite.
2. There is truth in the [horseshoe theory of politics](https://substack.com/redirect/50c31673-7945-48a3-b82a-57d61eb6e555?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), that the far left and far right are uncomfortably close on certain policy issues. That's particularly evident in the MAHA movement, as an example.
3. I do think this is a precarious moment in politics, because politics is reactionary.

We're living through an antiestablishment moment that's accelerating, and it's clear that _everyone_ across the ideological spectrum [thinks that our institutions are broken](https://substack.com/redirect/fce26cf4-60d1-466b-a1f0-cfe28ad1c15d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
**Moderates too often come across as incrementalists at a time when people want bigger change**. That doesn't have to be the case.
There are a lot of major reforms--infrastructure, housing costs, education, AI and workforce displacement--where moderate Democrats at the state and federal level are well positioned to lead. For any criticism it's faced, [the Abundance movement](https://substack.com/redirect/a9feeafc-82ca-4350-a3c0-5682271b8e78?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) is a pretty good example of this.
**The goal of government is to help people and make their lives better**. DOGE and the MAGA movement have spectacularly failed to do that.17 I'm not casting them as equivalents, but DSA electeds and electeds-to-be are also unserious legislators.
Bernie Sanders is famously ineffective; over 35 years in Congress, [he's been the lead sponsor of only three standalone bills that have passed](https://substack.com/redirect/9dcfdb21-f10f-40d6-a356-8fe28d8797fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)--two of which renamed post offices. Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib, the two DSA incumbents, have passed [zero laws as lead sponsors](https://substack.com/redirect/e3413035-33f4-4a14-bafc-5cd0b470db56?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), albeit in a shorter period of time.
That leaves it to the serious legislators--often the people winning in the toughest races with the broadest appeal--to get things done.

clean_body: But Democrats should be alarmed by candidates winning primaries on unworkable, unpopular platforms. | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more But Democrats should be alarmed by candidates winning primaries on unworkable, unpopular platforms. | | | Jul 8 | | | | | | | | | | If you pay way too much attention to politics, as I do,1 there's been a lot of coverage about how progressives--and members of the Democratic Socialists of America (DSA) specifically, who are to the left of progressives--have won a bunch of recent U.S. House primaries. It is true that DSA members unseated incumbents and . A few other things are true: 1. The DSA is among the general public, and moving to the left to placate a loud but small part of the base is a sure-fire way to lose some otherwise winnable general elections. 2. Even if DSA members win every competitive primary they're in for the rest of this cycle, they'd represent under 5% of the Democratic U.S. House caucus. 3. The media has done a terrible job covering trends in Democratic primaries, selectively extrapolating from a few elections in NYC. 4. Moderate Democrats are right to be worried about the direction of the party. Being moderate isn 't inconsistent with being ambitious. Moderate Democrats should be pushing for more ambitious reforms; but to do that, you need to run on policies that are popular enough to get you elected, and popular enough to garner support from Republicans. ? No, the DSA isn't taking over This was The Wall Street Journal opinion page late last week, with stories about socialism highlighted in red. | | ---|---|--- From the afternoon of July 2. It is true that no matter how the primaries play out over the next couple of months, the ranks of Democratic Socialists in the U.S. House will increase by multiples. But those multiples are off of a very, very small base. Right now, there are who are DSA members. That will increase to at least six2 in the next election; it may increase a bit more than that. Let's assume that the DSA, somehow, gets to 10 members of the U.S. House next session.3 Even in that scenario, which isn't particularly likely, DSA members will still make up less than 5% of the Democratic caucus,4 and 2.3% of the House as a whole. There are 435 members of the U.S. House; in any given year, there's no shortage of lunatics. A few more of them are adding a DSA label onto their lunacy, but that doesn't make it a takeover worthy of wall-to-wall WSJ coverage. The media's coverage of the DSA wins has been abysmal That the DSA is growing its ranks is, absolutely, a story. But based on the day-after coverage, you'd think it was a seismic change in the composition of the party. That's certainly how everyone in the press covered it: , , , , , , , , , , the list goes on. Part of this is that way too many reporters live in New York City, and as a result, NYC politics is chronically overcovered.5 Because the races below got a fraction of the media coverage, you may be unaware that on the very same night as the NYC primaries: 1. , the 32-year-old Maryland delegate,6 against far more progressive candidates. He's now running in a safe Democratic seat and will almost certainly win in November. 2. , a former member of the centrist Blue Dogs in the U.S. House, handily won a primary for a safe Democratic seat against Bernie Sanders-endorsed state senator . 3. Most importantly, less than an hour up the road from NYC,7 moderate won in a swing seat held by Mike Lawler, a Republican.8 Why is this most important? Because if you care about Democrats actually winning back the House, then Democrats should nominate moderate candidates. DSA-aligned candidates do terribly in general elections. DSA nominees do really poorly in general elections All of the elections I've written about above are primaries, not general elections. That's notable because the . Here's how candidates endorsed by Justice Democrats and Our Revolution, groups in the same ideological lane as the DSA, perform in general elections.9 | | ---|---|--- For all that people talk about the polarization of politics, candidate quality still matters, and people are less likely to vote for candidates they see as extreme.10 That won't matter in the races with DSA nominees because they're all in extremely Democratic seats--even underperforming candidates won't cost Democrats those elections.11 But there are are competitive12--and if Democrats want to win back the House, the political alignment of candidates matters a great deal. To date, Democrats have done a decent job of this, nominating more electable House candidates in , and a few seats in . That hasn't been universally true--Democrats nominated a weaker candidate in a the consistent media narrative isn't exactly backed by what's been happening outside of New York City. There are still primaries to go--Cori Bush is running against Wesley Bell in Missouri-01 again,14 and the Democrats may very well nominate a | | | | | | | ---|---|--- | July 24, 2024 | But no, the DSA hasn't taken over the Democratic Party. With that said: if the party fails to distance itself from DSA impulses, it will cost Democrats at the ballot box, something in 2020.16 What should we learn from recent primaries? Let me say three things here: 1. I don't believe there is an equivalency between DSA leadership and MAGA leadership. I strenuously object to a lot of what the DSA says, does, and believes. But I don't believe that there's the same anti-democracy instinct, willingness to subvert laws, or that's evidently a Trump administration prerequisite. 2. There is truth in the , that the far left and far right are uncomfortably close on certain policy issues. That's particularly evident in the MAHA movement, as an example. 3. I do think this is a precarious moment in politics, because politics is reactionary. We're living through an antiestablishment moment that's accelerating, and it's clear that everyone across the ideological spectrum . Moderates too often come across as incrementalists at a time when people want bigger change. That doesn't have to be the case. There are a lot of major reforms--infrastructure, housing costs, education, AI and workforce displacement--where moderate Democrats at the state and federal level are well positioned to lead. For any criticism it's faced, is a pretty good example of this. The goal of government is to help people and make their lives better. DOGE and the MAGA movement have spectacularly failed to do that.17 I'm not casting them as equivalents, but DSA electeds and electeds-to-be are also unserious legislators. Bernie Sanders is famously ineffective; over 35 years in Congress, of which renamed post offices. Reps. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez and Rashida Tlaib, the two DSA incumbents, have passed , albeit in a shorter period of time. That leaves it to the serious legislators--often the people winning in the toughest races with the broadest appeal--to get things done. ? In an R+10 district that rates as Safe Republican, a candidate whose issues include "" is perhaps not very likely to win that seat. 4 Obviously, it depends on how many Democrats win seats. If Democrats win 210 seats, then the DSA will make up 4.8% of the caucus. If Democrats win 218 seats (the minimum needed for a majority), then the DSA will make up 4.6% of the caucus. If Democrats win 230 seats, then the DSA will make up 4.3% of the caucus. 5 On the other hand, it's not like Missouri doesn't have its share of . 6 , , and have "Houses of Delegates" rather than "Houses of Representatives." But it's the same thing in practice. 7 Well, it depends where in NYC you're driving from. But it's still perfectly plausible that wins that race, which makes it very possible that the Democrats lose that seat. I also wrote this before all of the broke in Maine. Peter, Last week, we celebrated the idea that freedom is worth fighting for. But freedom isn't just political. **It's also personal.** And for many Americans, the financial aspect of freedom is the one that's slipping the furthest out of reach. That's exactly what we dug into during _**How to Protect & Grow Your American Dream,**_ and if you haven't watched it yet, it's still available. [Watch the replay here](https://xtz223.keap-link008.com/v2/click/660639ad148d582de23b485e3512333e/eJyNkM1qwzAQhN9FZ1Pr15YMpYQQgnGaQ2nPQbLWVCSWhaOEusHvXqUpObXQ6-7stzNzQRG89rG2qEIf8ZNShjI0QuuCAx-Xg4-6_d5SwQkjGTo4v1-Pwymg6vLr8V1wHStS0AzFKUCSvL4slk29Xe829bZJyqDH9ONfHFlSeeesnhf1Bs3zn2DoXVydE_uIqjie4JrIupQqvo2HpH-PMRyrPD-7HoaHduhzQnGBOWdE5NQIDKTUvHxyvtu1twp2e5gejaIlFBowxxpjzInGUhmhtDAGpCTEYM063FkGIKwynHWG8bYoCONK2jJZ0yGAtz-9NjDdDM5f5S16uQ==) **Bill Spadea** opened his segment with something that stuck with a lot of people on the call. His point went far beyond politics. It was about personal responsibility and financial ownership. Neither political party is coming to fix your finances for you. That responsibility and that power sits with you. The average business owner overpays by $11K a year in taxes. Not because they're doing anything wrong, but because nobody ever showed them a better structure. Tax filing tells you what already happened. Tax planning asks a completely different question: how can the same dollars create reduction, growth, income, and legacy, all at once. That's the real definition of freedom we talked about in the training. Not just flags and fireworks, but the ability to keep more of what you earn, build wealth on your own terms, and stop financing everyone else's freedom before your own. Lead Story · Iran & NATO
U.S. HITS IRAN AGAIN AND REIMPOSES OIL SANCTIONS — AS TRUMP BERATES NATO ALLIES IN ANKARA
What's Happening
The U.S. military launched what Central Command called a **series of powerful strikes** on more than 80 Iranian targets Tuesday, after Iran fired on three commercial ships in Omani waters near the Strait of Hormuz — a move Washington branded a **“gross violation”** of the ceasefire. The administration also reimposed sanctions on Iranian oil, and Brent crude jumped about 5%. President Trump ordered the strike from Ankara, Turkey, where he is attending the NATO summit.
The Situation
* Trump convened his top team — Rubio, Hegseth, Treasury’s Bessent and Joint Chiefs Chairman Gen. Dan Caine — in Ankara to approve the plan. He had warned that if Iran broke the deal, the U.S. would **“go right back to dropping bombs.”**
* At the summit, Trump is pressing allies toward a **5% of GDP** defense benchmark and is openly furious that Spain, Italy and initially the UK denied bases or airspace for Operation Epic Fury against Iran. He has again dismissed NATO as a **“paper tiger.”**
* In a sharp reversal, Trump said he will **lift sanctions on Turkey** and revive the long-stalled F-35 sale to Ankara — years after Turkey was expelled from the program over its Russian missile-defense purchase. Israel’s Netanyahu objected, calling Erdogan “not exactly a model ally.”
* Reimposing oil sanctions scraps one of the central concessions that had reopened Hormuz. The funeral-week “pause” Trump had granted Tehran is over.

The Perspective
This is deterrence with a return address. Iran tested the ceasefire by shooting at ships, and within hours it absorbed 80-plus targets and lost its oil-sanctions relief — that is what a credible red line looks like, and it’s a world away from the “strongly worded letter” era. Trump’s needling of freeloading allies also lands harder when Washington just did the fighting Europe refused to. The honest caveats: Brent up 5% means the pump-and-grocery relief families just started feeling could reverse, and re-escalation is exactly the outcome Trump said he wanted to avoid. The ceasefire is now hanging by a thread.

Justice · Utah
THE MAN ACCUSED OF ASSASSINATING CHARLIE KIRK FACES HIS VICTIM’S FAMILY AS HEARING OPENS
What's Happening
Tyler Robinson, 23, sat in a Provo, Utah courtroom this week for the opening of a five-day preliminary hearing over the September 10 assassination of **Charlie Kirk** — the Turning Point USA founder and Trump ally shot while speaking at Utah Valley University. It was the first time Kirk’s widow, Erika, and his parents saw Robinson in person; Donald Trump Jr. sat in the gallery.
The Situation
* Robinson faces **aggravated murder** — a capital charge — plus firearm, obstruction and witness-tampering counts. Prosecutors are seeking the **death penalty**. He has not entered a plea.
* Judge Tony Graf will decide whether there is enough evidence to send the case to trial. Prosecutors are laying out surveillance, doorbell and bystander video placing Robinson at the scene; the judge initially blocked footage the defense said had been altered with zooms and blurs.
* Investigators testified that Robinson allegedly confessed by text to his partner and left a note, with a purported motive tied to Kirk’s public views — a message that he’d **“had enough of his hatred.”**
* Kirk’s family called each proceeding “a painful reminder”; Erika Kirk and Kirk’s parents stood and walked out during testimony describing the shooting.

The Perspective
Ten months on, the case against Kirk’s accused killer is being built in painstaking — and at times clumsy — detail, a reminder that due process grinds slowly even when the evidence looks overwhelming. The wrangling over altered video is the system working, not failing; better to fix it now than hand an appeal later. But don’t lose the thread beneath the procedure: a young conservative was gunned down for making arguments in public, and his family is now forced to relive it frame by frame. That’s where the attention belongs.
[Read the full story at the Deseret News](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/RUdnyxJ8qj1K4ftAiLwzyuOuarLVp%2Fwo%2BMbm9DCmqkgFnkb4EsEXIfiaAZsC%0AGSyV1%2FQyokZ%2Bi4u8zWLtsspqHZvXV2phpksnXxyPT%2B49h2tQwA0yUWzQDlK7%0AaEYHue%2BrFLQm%2BeOlpC85Pw0axT26ZHb0Kk2zFwEqRoAFyOoEaoC%2B7amt6Mp8%0A3nlhrSzg42pJamYUZhhMPxjfVFZo8zujtA%3D%3D%0A/39b81a2bf7133f3e)
The Economy
WALMART SLASHES PRICES ON BEEF, SODA AND SUMMER STAPLES — AND TRUMP CLAIMS THE CREDIT
What's Happening
Walmart and Sam’s Club cut prices this week on thousands of items — ground beef by roughly 12–15%, 24-packs of Coke and Pepsi by 33% and 29%, plus corn, cherries, ice cream, chips, even grills and sunscreen — pitched as summer savings. Trump posted that the cuts came **“at my Administration’s request”** for the country’s 250th birthday and praised Walmart as a “truly patriotic Company.”
The Situation
* Walmart’s own statement framed the rollbacks as helping customers “make the most” of summer and made **no mention** of Trump or any White House request; the company declined to comment on his claim.
* The backdrop is real pocketbook pain: the Consumer Price Index is up **4.2%** over the past year — the hottest reading in more than three years — driven higher by energy costs from the Iran war.
* Analysts called it a “win/win”: affordability messaging for Trump heading into the midterms, and the low-price spotlight for Walmart.
* Some relief had come from the Iran ceasefire lowering oil — but that is now in doubt after Tuesday’s U.S. strikes and reimposed sanctions sent crude up about 5%.

The Perspective
Lower stickers on beef and Coke are a real, tangible win heading into cookout season, and a retailer using its scale to drive prices down is capitalism doing what no politician can order by decree. On the credit fight, be straight: Walmart pointedly declined to confirm the “at my request” line, so take it with salt. And the timing is awkward — the same week prices ease at the shelf, the Iran flare-up threatens to shove energy, and food, right back up. Bank this win before the next oil spike eats it.
[Read the full story at Fox Business](https://link.mail.beehiiv.com/v1/c/Luztw1Tdn9MRHdDzjIGhhvY4uEcaRfIU84T%2FAi1TiGTeVyhvnvluQeRqwAci%0At7JubSPaYQ%2BpcQKcQBlH0HfbCPPD16IyyAhxTT3hbfyEwPhI8JconazdeqK6%0ALokf14lV7z%2F%2BJyqIGfOAoCEM5vWWJo2%2FNZ2JbwKsQL0H6%2FRcHaM20BokTrak%0AoEFiM7KmzyXwXhdI%2BOonsWp2nWTEoWDWuQ%3D%3D%0A/2f4c3dfeee963582)
The World · Syria
BOMBS GREET MACRON IN DAMASCUS AS THE WEST BETS ON SYRIA’S EX-JIHADIST PRESIDENT
What's Happening
Two improvised bombs went off near the Four Seasons hotel in Damascus on Tuesday, wounding 18 people including four police officers, just as French President **Emmanuel Macron** — the first Western leader to visit post-Assad Syria — arrived to meet Syrian President **Ahmed al-Sharaa**. Macron’s motorcade had left the hotel minutes earlier and he was unharmed.
The Situation
* Syrian authorities said the crude devices — one in a parked car, one in a trash can — were planted outside Macron’s security cordon and detonated as forces tried to defuse them. No group claimed responsibility, though **ISIS** has stepped up attacks on al-Sharaa’s government this year.
* It was the second and third blast in Damascus in a week; a cafe bombing days earlier killed nine to ten people.
* Al-Sharaa — a former al-Qaeda-linked commander who toppled Bashar al-Assad in 2024 — gave Macron a lavish reception and pitched France as a **“primary partner,”** bringing in the chiefs of TotalEnergies and shipping giant CMA CGM.

name: Defenders of Wildlife
subject: Say welcome back to bison, America’s national mammal!
body:
How much do you know about American bison?
How much do you know about American bison?

## _America’s national mammal, plain and simple!_
* * *
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What’s the story with America’s bison?_**
Bison are synonymous with the Plains – massive, shaggy herds of bulls, cows and calves grazing across the grasslands since time immemorial. Once numbering in the millions, bison now occupy a much smaller portion of their historic habitat, but year after year new calves are born that carry on the bison’s legacy. Slowly but surely, bison are returning to the Great Plains.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_Where are the bison today?_**
The wild herds roaming around Yellowstone National Park are descendants of the last remaining bison that were almost wiped out in the 19th century. Today, bison are coming back from the brink, but make no mistake, their numbers are growing!
#
Bison are special: As they graze, they spread native grass seeds and create nutritious forage that benefits many prairie herbivores. Restoring these animals is a way to right the wrongs of the past and maintain healthy prairie habitat for a host of plains wildlife!
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_What’s been happening with the bison comeback?_**
Together, Native American communities and conservation groups are delivering bison success stories. In one example, just last year, [**a family group of Yellowstone bison**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5730630/38SyG9Xl) were gifted from the Fort Peck Assiniboine and Sioux Tribes in Montana to the Mosquito, Grizzly Bears’ Head and Lean Man First Nations in Canada. Their return is helping Tribal Nations heal and reconnect to this culturally significant animal.
#
|
---
| | |
---
#
#### **_How can we help?_**
[**Defenders has been in court defending Yellowstone’s bison herd against legal challenges**](https://support.defenders.org/s/5730631/38SyG9Xl) , and we’re supporting programs that divert bison from slaughter and transfer them to Tribal lands across the West. You can help by supporting our efforts, and by telling your friends and family what you know about the miraculous return of bison!
#
|
---
[Discover more ongoing bison!](https://support.defenders.org/s/5730632/38SyG9Xl)
---
| | |
---
