Iran and Ceasefire Trump says MOU is "over," warns U.S. will hit Iran again: President Donald Trump reporters in Ankara on Wednesday that he thought the memorandum of understanding between the the U.S. and Iran was "over," following the trade of strikes between the two countries (see below), adding that "dealing" with the Iranians was "just a waste of time." He warned that attacks on Iran will continue on Wednesday night and that the U.S. is going to "hit them hard tonight." In the remarks that preceded this announcement, Trump said that the U.S. had "hit Iran very hard last night," called the Iranians "evil people," and insisted the attacks were part of the U.S. campaign to "denuclearise" Iran, which does not possess nuclear weapons. Trump also registered his discontent with NATO for insufficient assistance during the U.S.-Israeli war on Iran. He said he was "not happy" with the organization "because of the fact that they didn't want to help us with the number one state-sponsored terror, that's Iran." Attacks hit tankers in the Strait of Hormuz: Two tankers were in separate attacks while transiting the Strait of Hormuz on Tuesday, according to the United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations Centre (UKMTO). In the first incident, a tanker was struck by an unidentified projectile. The vessel is believed to have sustained structural damage, but no casualties or environmental impact were reported. At 1:05 p.m. UTC, UKMCO received a report of a second attack in which another tanker was struck by an unidentified aerial vehicle. The tanker sustained minor structural damage, with no casualties or pollution reported, and continued to its next port of call. Both incidents occurred in the same general area off the coast of Oman. They followed a similar attack on Monday, in which a Qatari tanker carrying liquefied natural gas was hit. Iran's military did not claim responsibility for any of the attacks, though it has insisted that it manages the Strait under the MOU, vessels have to pass through the northern corridor managed by Iran, and any attempts to bypass its route or escape detection are a violation of the agreement. Qatar and Saudi Arabia both issued formal statements on Tuesday describing the targeting of their vessels and holding Iran accountable for the strikes. U.S. strikes Iran: In response to the vessel strikes, which it called a violation of the ceasefire, U.S. Central Command announced new strikes on Iran. Multiple explosions were overnight near the Iranian coastal cities of Sirik and Qeshm, on Kharg Island, and in other locations along the Strait of Hormuz, according to Mehr News, an Iranian state-affiliated outlet. Bandar Abbas was also reportedly hit. A later estimate from CENTCOM claimed that "over 80" locations had been targeted, "including air defense systems, command and control networks, and coastal radar sites," and that they had disabled "over 60" small boats used by Iran's navy. According to Iranian media, however, most of these strikes hit civilian areas, and shrapnel from one attack, near Sirik's commercial pier, reportedly wounded several civilians. Other sites struck included fishing piers and a telecommunications tower, Iranian media reported. A U.S. official the strikes as "punishment, not proportional" to CNN. Iran vows "crushing response," strikes U.S. military bases in Kuwait and Bahrain: the repeated violations by the U.S. of the Islamabad memorandum of understanding, particularly the violations of its first clause with Israel's continuing assault on Lebanon, and following the strikes, Iran's Foreign Ministry announced it would take "any action it deems necessary" to protect its interests and national security. Iran's Khatam-al-Anbiya Central Headquarters also condemned the strikes as a "blatant act of aggression," noting that they occurred during the funeral procession for Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei, who was killed in February by an Israeli strike, and warning that Iran's military would deliver a "crushing response" to the attacks. Air raid sirens were reported in Kuwait and Bahrain, with authorities in both countries releasing statements saying their air defenses were actively intercepting and destroying Iranian missiles and drones. The IRGC said in a statement that it had struck 85 military facilities in the Persian Gulf, including the U.S. Fifth Fleet Headquarters at Bahrain's Salman Port and its Sheikh Isa Air Base, as well as the Ali Al Salem base in Kuwait. U.S. reimposes sanctions on Iranian oil: Earlier on Tuesday, and following strikes on vessels in Hormuz, the U.S. Treasury Department announced it would be reimposing sanctions on Iranian oil that were lifted by the signing of the memorandum of understanding. The sanctions will go into effect on July 17, according to the statement, which announced their resumption. Oil prices more than 5% following the announcement. Khamenei funeral procession reaches Iraq: The body of Ayatollah Khamenei in Najaf, Iraq, where it was received with full state honors by Iraq's top leadership, including Shia, Sunni, Kurdish, Christian, and other political and religious representatives, Drop Site's Sarmad Jawad reported. Some Iraqi MPs were heard chanting "Death to America. Death to Israel." Iraq is hosting an official state funeral for the former Iranian Supreme Leader, with millions of Iraqis expected to line the streets to pay their respects. U.S. commanders bypassed outdated intelligence warnings before deadly Iran school strike : Senior U.S. military commanders database warnings that intelligence on Iranian targets was severely outdated before approving strikes on the war's first day, including one that hit the Shajareh Tayyiba girls' school in Minab, killing at least 168 children and 14 teachers, according to a new report from CNN. According to the report, analysts prioritized updating records for "upper-tier" mobile threats like missile sites before the war began, leaving fixed sites such as the school reliant on intelligence over 10 years old in the Pentagon's MIDB and MARS targeting databases, sources said. The override preceding approval was reportedly driven by pressure from senior Pentagon leadership to supply targets quickly. Lebanon Israeli airstrikes hit Nabatieh, southern villages overnight: Israeli warplanes the Ali Al-Taher woodland near Nabatieh El-Fawqah around 2 a.m. local time on Wednesday, following artillery shelling in the area, Lebanon's National News Agency reported. Israeli aircraft also carried out three waves of strikes between Beit Yahoun, Kounine and Braachit overnight, while drones were reported flying intensively over Tyre and Beirut's southern suburbs earlier in the day. Aoun condemns Iran 's retaliatory attacks: Lebanese President Joseph Aoun on Wednesday Iranian attacks targeting Bahrain and Kuwait as violations of their sovereignty and international law, per Lebanon's National News Agency, though he made no similar condemnations of the earlier U.S. attacks on Iran. Earlier on Tuesday, a White House official told Reuters that Trump had invited Lebanese President Joseph Aoun to visit the White House on July 21. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, eight Palestinians were killed and 17 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza. Two bodies were also recovered from under the rubble, according to the Palestinian Health Ministry. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,110 killed, with 173,599 injured, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,084 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,491, while 799 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel kills six Palestinians, including two children, on Wednesday: Six Palestinians, including two children, were in Israeli attacks on Khan Younis and Gaza City in Gaza on Wednesday afternoon, WAFA reported. Four people, including a 10-year-old child, were killed when an Israeli airstrike hit a tent at Al-Saada camp south of Khan Younis. In Gaza City, one Palestinian was killed in an Israeli airstrike west of the city, while another child was shot dead by Israeli forces in the Zeitoun neighborhood southeast of Gaza City. Israeli attacks on Tuesday kill five in Gaza: Two Israeli airstrikes on Tel Al-Hawa neighborhood south of Gaza City two, including a child, and injured four others Tuesday evening, the Palestinian Red Crescent Society reported. Another strike on a vehicle in Al-Sabra neighborhood killed four, including two children. Israel shoots, detains Palestinian man at Bethlehem checkpoint : Israeli forces a Palestinian man in the thigh with live ammunition at a military checkpoint between Bethlehem and Jerusalem on Wednesday before detaining him, according to WAFA. Israeli airstrike kills Egyptian Relief Committee worker organizing World Cup match screenings: Israel struck and Mohammed Fawaz Al-Wahidi, an employee of the Egyptian Relief Committee in Gaza, hitting a vehicle in Gaza City about an hour before the World Cup match between Egypt and Argentina. The strike killed three others, including two children. The committee had been organizing public screenings of World Cup matches for displaced families across the Strip. A later statement from the committee, which identified Al-Wahidi and noted his role as a respected community leader, said he was on his way to a neighborhood reconciliation meeting when he was killed. UN warns of chickenpox surge in Gaza amid overcrowding and collapsing sanitation: Nearly 9,300 chickenpox infections were over the past two weeks in Gaza, more than half of them in the southern area of Khan Younis, the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA) reported. OCHA attributed the outbreak to deteriorating environmental conditions, severe overcrowding, poor sanitation, and the summer season. The surge comes as around 1.7 million forcibly displaced Palestinians are living across more than 1,600 displacement sites. It added that 83% of assessed displacement sites have reported rodent and parasite infestations, while the collapsing health system continues to face critical shortages of essential medical supplies amid Israeli restrictions. Palestinian rights group accuses Israeli prison staff of attempted killing of detainee : The Palestinian Prisoners' Society said Wednesday that Israeli prison officials deliberately attempted to kill Palestinian prisoner Ghassan Ibrahim Zwahra, citing his testimony of being shot with rubber-coated bullets on multiple occasions after his June 8 transfer to Negev Prison, according to WAFA. Zwahra was also subjected to humiliating strip searches, brutal beatings, and was unable to walk as a result of his injuries, ultimately losing consciousness in the prison yard, which necessitated hospitalization, the group says. Zwahra, who has spent 17 years in Israeli prisons, was re-detained in February 2025. Only seven of these years were a result of actual sentences; the remaining 10 were spent in "administrative detention," whereby Israel can summarily subject Palestinians to detentions of indefinite length without criminal charges or a trial. U.S. politicians call for the release of Gaza physician: Sen. Chris Van Hollen for the immediate release of detained Gaza pediatrician Dr. Hussam Abu Safiya on Tuesday, noting that Dr. Abu Safiya has spent 18 months in Israeli detention without charge or trial. Darializa Avila Chevalier, who recently won a high-profile race in New York's Democratic Primary and is expected to win a seat in the U.S. House of Representatives, joined Van Hollen in calling for Dr. Abu Safiya's immediate release. Chevalier that in Congress she would "fight tooth and nail" to cease the "endless endless flow of weapons and American taxpayer dollars" to Israel, noting its egregious violations of international humanitarian law and its multifront war against its neighbors and rivals. The UN Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem also demanded the immediate and unconditional release of Abu Safiya. The commission warned in a on Wednesday that Abu Safiya's deteriorating health was the direct result of "continued and severe abuse since his detention by the Israeli authorities in December 2024." The commission added that Israel's treatment of Abu Safiya reflected a broader pattern: "Israeli security forces deliberately killed, wounded, detained, and severely mistreated medical personnel, constituting the war crimes of wilful killing and torture and the crime against humanity of extermination." Hind Rajab Foundation files criminal complaint against Israeli in Italy: The Belgium-based Hind Rajab Foundation a criminal complaint on Tuesday, pointing Italian prosecutors towards Israeli citizen Arik Ben Asulin, who the group says is currently in Italy. The foundation says he participated in war crimes, crimes against humanity, and acts of genocide while serving in the Israeli military's 749th Combat Engineering Battalion in Gaza. The complaint cites his alleged role in the destruction of the Netzarim Corridor, Al-Azhar University, and Gaza City's Shujaiya neighborhood, relying on satellite imagery, U.N. findings, investigative reporting, and Ben Asulin's own social media posts. CPJ reconsidering its removal of killed Palestinian journalists from its database: The Committee to Protect Journalists is reconsidering its removal of four Palestinian journalists killed in Gaza from its casualty database, the Electronic Intifada reported Wednesday, after a major controversy roiled the organization last week when it considered changing its definition of who is a journalist to exclude "state-backed propaganda outlets" or other outlets affiliated with "armed groups," a change it ultimately did not make. CPJ is reportedly reviewing the cases of three journalists from Press House Palestine, all killed by Israel within the first few months of the Gaza genocide, one of whom was recognized as a journalist by UNESCO. The organization was also profiled by the Guardian, with one of these journalists, Mohammed Al-Jaja, described as having "his Press House flak jacket and press card resting on top of his body," after he was killed. Read the full report from the Electronic Intifada . U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. Fallout from accusations against Graham Platner continues: New allegations: Lyndsey Fifield , the ex-girlfriend whose allegations of physical abuse against Graham Platner anchored last month's New York Times story, now tells the Washington Post he removed condoms during sex without her consent at least six times while they dated from 2013 to 2015, knowing she was not on birth control. "He would do it in a sneaky way," she said. A close friend said Fifield told her about it when the relationship ended, according to the Post. Platner denied the claims and noted Fifield's "well-documented political agenda." Fifield is a longtime Republican operative who worked for the Heritage Foundation and Nikki Haley 's campaign, and publicly defended Brett Kavanaugh against sexual assault allegations. Troy Jackson files paperwork indicating he might run: Former Maine Senate President Troy Jackson the first Democrat to formally take steps to replace current nominee Graham Platner, filing paperwork on Tuesday with the Federal Election Commission to form a U.S. Senate exploratory committee, according to the Bangor Daily News. The filing allows Jackson to raise money before announcing a campaign. Read more on Troy Jackson and his support from former Platner volunteers in this report from Drop Site contributor Nathan Bernard. Nirav Shah also announces intention to run : Nirav Shah , a former gubernatorial candidate and public health official, on Tuesday he was preparing to enter the race should Platner withdraw, calling for an "open and transparent process" to decide the new nominee, including at least one televised debate and multiple town halls across the state. Shah said he would run on Medicare for All, increasing taxes on the wealthy, reproductive rights, and challenging Trump, but did not mention Palestine. Shah's 2026 gubernatorial campaign received more than $630,000 in support from 314 Action Fund, an AIPAC-linked Super PAC. Sanders urges Platner to drop out: Sen. Bernie Sanders (I-Vt.) posted on X Tuesday that he had "spoken with Platner" and had "recommended that he step aside." ICE officer kills Mexican immigrant during Houston traffic stop : An ICE officer shot and Lorenzo Salgado Araujo in Houston's Magnolia Park neighborhood on Tuesday. The agency accused Araujo of ramming into an ICE vehicle and refusing verbal commands during an attempted arrest. Salgado Araujo's family said he had lived in the U.S. for nearly 35 years and was in the process of obtaining legal status, according to his son Ronaldo Salgado. The** League of United Latin American Citizens said Salgado Araujo was picking up employees in a work vehicle at the time of the stop, and the group's chief executive called for a city police investigation while offering a $5,000 reward for more information about the shooting. Rep. Thomas Massie says he will reintroduce NDAA amendment: Rep. Thomas Massie (R-Ky.) on Tuesday he would again offer his amendment to strip Section 219 from the NDAA when the House reconvenes July 13. The Section 219 provision would integrate U.S. and Israeli military technology across weapons co-production, AI, cyber, and data-sharing. Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu has called the provision his personal plan. The Rules Committee blocked the bipartisan Massie-Khanna amendment to this provision last week without debate, keeping it from a floor vote. But the procedural measure needed to bring the NDAA itself to the floor then unexpectedly failed, stalling the whole bill and forcing the committee to write a new rule, giving opponents of the provision another shot. DOJ threatens criminal prosecution over noncitizen voting in letters to all 50 states : The Justice Department's civil rights division, led by Harmeet Dhillon , letters Tuesday to election officials in all 50 states and Washington, D.C., warning that officials could face possible criminal liability if noncitizens are found on voter rolls or to have cast ballots. The letters are part of President Donald Trump's ongoing push to tighten election restrictions, though there is no evidence of widespread noncitizen voting. The DOJ gave officials five days to detail their compliance efforts, though the letters carry no formal subpoena power. Also on Tuesday, the DOJ notified Detroit, Lansing, and East Lansing that federal monitors would observe the upcoming Michigan primary, alleging issues in the 2024 election; Detroit City Clerk Janice Winfrey characterized these as "false assertions" used to exert special power over Detroit, a city with a heavy Black majority. Lawsuit alleges U.S. shared confidential asylum data with Iranian government : A lawsuit Tuesday in U.S. District Court in Washington, D.C., alleges that U.S. immigration agencies shared confidential asylum records of detained Iranians with the Iranian government, violating federal confidentiality regulations, according to court filings from the Iranian American Legal Defense Fund and Public Citizen Litigation Group. The complaint claims State Department officials arranged monthly meetings with Iranian officials starting in March 2025, using the Pakistani embassy as an intermediary, to share sensitive details about detainees the U.S. sought to deport. The lawsuit alleges the shared information included asylum details from people who said they were persecuted in Iran for converting to Christianity, their sexuality, or participation in the 2022 Women, Life, Freedom protests, with disclosures reportedly continuing even after U.S.-Israeli strikes on Iran began the war in February 2026. About 600 Iranians were placed in immigration detention last year, according to public records obtained by the National Iranian American Council, and three deportation flights returned dozens of Iranians to Iran between September 2025 and January 2026, with some deportees reportedly including asylum seekers. Democratic nominee Valdez says she would support sanctions on Israel: Congressional candidate and current New York Rep. Claire Valdez she would "absolutely" support sanctions on Israel similar to those imposed on South Africa, BreakThrough News reported. "We have a lot of tools at our disposal, including diplomatic tools," she said, adding that "we should be looking at those tools now." Other International News Trump again threatens to cut off all trade with Spain: As part of his remarks at Wednesday's NATO summit in Ankara,** President Donald Trump that he had directed U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to "cut off" all trade with Spain, calling it a "terrible partner" in the Atlantic alliance. In March, Trump also told Bessent to cut off trade with Spain, after Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez announced that Spain would not allow the U.S. to use its bases for operations against Iran, calling strikes by Israel and the U.S. on Iran "reckless and illegal." Sanchez has also been a vocal critic of Israel during its genocide in Gaza, calling it a "genocidal state" and indicating that Spain could not "do business" with such a country. Trump revives Greenland acquisition push, threatens to pull U.S. troops from Europe : President Trump on Tuesday calls for the U.S. to acquire Greenland, saying the territory "should be controlled by the United States" and suggesting Washington could withdraw all its troops from Europe over the continent's resistance to the idea. Speaking in Ankara ahead of Wednesday's NATO summit, Trump blamed the Greenland dispute for damaging his relationship with NATO and repeated unverified claims about Chinese and Russian ships near the island. Finnish President Alexander Stubb responded to Trump's comments by emphasizing NATO's existing Arctic capabilities, noting that Finland has trained a million soldiers in Arctic conditions and that seven alliance members are Arctic nations. A U.S., Danish, and Greenlandic working group has been meeting on the territory's status since Trump and NATO Secretary General Mark Rutte reportedly reached a preliminary "framework" agreement in late January, with Danish Foreign Minister Lars Lokke Rasmussen saying he expects a resolution by year's end. United Nations approves extraordinary session on U.S. sanctions on Cuba : Over U.S. objections, the UN General Assembly 136-9 on Tuesday to hold an extraordinary session, requested by Cuba, to address an escalation in the U.S. sanctions regime on the island and its effect on Cuba's energy infrastructure. Cuba's Foreign Minister Bruno Rodriguez told the session that the U.S. is waging a "multidimensional, unconventional war" against Cuba, now in its seventh decade and "more brutal and ruthless in the last seven months," with an energy siege "equivalent to a naval blockade, which is an act of war." He called U.S. policy, which caused yet another islandwide blackout on Monday, "collective punishment" enforced against Cuba's population, and estimated it had cost the nation $8 billion from March 2025 to February 2026. The U.S. had lobbied other countries at the UN to join its effort to block the debate entirely; only the U.S., Israel, Argentina, and six others voted against the extraordinary session. The UN has passed a non-binding resolution calling for the lifting of the U.S. blockade every year since 1992, with the support of a large majority of its member states. Marine Le Pen to run in 2027 election: Far-right French politician Marine Le Pen that she would run in France's 2027 presidential election on Tuesday, following a decision by a Paris appeals court upholding her embezzlement conviction that allows her to seek public office once again. Le Pen, who has long headed the far-right French National Rally (formerly "National Front") party, was found guilty of embezzling €2.8 million in European Parliament funds. She was banned from pursuing elected office by the court, but Tuesday's ruling reduced that ban, effectively allowing her to run in the 2027 election. It also mandated that Le Pen wear an ankle monitor in lieu of her suspended jail sentence, which Le Pen has said would make campaigning impossible. She is appealing the decision to France's highest court, which automatically suspends the sentence until a final ruling is issued. Drone strikes kill 15 in Sudan: At least 15 civilians were in two separate strikes on vehicles on Monday and Tuesday in Sudan's North Kordofan region, the Sudanese human rights group Emergency Lawyers reported. The largest of these attacks, on a vehicle in the town of Al-Shatoot, killed 13 civilians, five of them women, according to the group. Kordofan has seen an escalation in drone strikes in recent weeks, with schools, hospitals, and water infrastructure in the region all sustaining serious damage. Dozens of policemen and 11 soldiers killed in southwest Pakistan : Insurgents killed 18 police officers and 11 soldiers, according to the Pakistan military. The policemen had been abducted Monday, when militants attacked police in the Ziarat district in Baluchistan province, the AP . Nine police officers were initially killed in that attack. A Pakistani military spokesperson said security forces had killed 54 insurgents. Right-wing Brazilian presidential candidate asks Trump for tariff relief: Right-wing Brazilian senator and presidential candidate Flavio Bolsonaro on Tuesday against a 25% tariff on his country to the U.S. Trade Representative, asserting that its trade practices, particularly an instant payment system, were not unfair, and noting the possible effects of the tariffs on the October election. The tariffs were proposed to derail the trial of former President Jair Bolsonaro, but the younger Bolsonaro fears they could be used against him in his campaign against incumbent President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva who has seen his popularity boosted after diplomatic spats with Washington. Russian strikes on Kyiv kill one, wound others: Russian forces Kyiv overnight Tuesday--the third time Russia has bombed the capital in less than a week--killing a woman and wounding two others, according to city officials. Ukrainian defenses were able to intercept most of Russia's drone attacks but not the ballistic missiles it launched, according to the country's air force. Other attacks were reported in the southern region of Mykolaiv, the eastern region of Dnipropetrovsk, and the southeastern city of Zaporizhzhia, the first of which killed a mother and daughter. Several others were wounded in both attacks. The attacks come as Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy presses for additional military support during this week's NATO summit in Ankara. U.S. charges gang leader in murder of Indian Sikh activist: The U.S. Lawrence Bishnoi, an imprisoned leader of an Indian gang, and a deputy, Satinderjeet Singh, with directing the 2023 murder of Hardeep Singh Nijjar, a Sikh nationalist leader killed in Vancouver, Canada, according to an indictment unsealed on Tuesday. The indictment claims that Bishnoi directed the murder from his prison cell in India, using a smuggled cellphone and providing a co-conspirator with a picture of and addresses for Nijjar. Nijjar's killing caused a diplomatic rift between the Canadian and Indian governments, with then-Prime Minister Justin Trudeau alleging that he had "credible evidence" linking the killing to Indian government agents. The U.S. indictment makes no such connections. Bombing suspect found shot dead in Ukraine: Anastasiia Berezovska, a 39-year-old Ukrainian national suspected of attempting to kill a prominent businessman in Monaco in a bombing attack last week, was near Kyiv on Tuesday, according to Ukraine's Security Services. Berezovska was reportedly shot in the head by a Ukrainian military intelligence officer, the Guardian reported. French prosecutors accuse Berezovska of receiving payments in cryptocurrency from two different men to kill Vadym Iermolaiev, a Ukrainian businessman who holds Cypriot citizenship and allegedly has close ties to Russia. State of Maine welfare fraud investigators have been quietly investigating the wife of disgraced progressive icon and alleged rapist Graham Platner for defrauding the Medicaid program, according to records obtained by _The Robinson Report_.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/224cf655-423b-4630-a447-ca5094143062?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
The documents, provided by a source who asked to remain anonymous, show alleged welfare overpayments totaling more than $9,000 in Medicaid benefits, known in Maine as MaineCare.
The records, from a "Fraud Investigation Recovery" case opened under Incident #2511-014, list Amy J. Gertner, Platner's wife, as the suspect and Platner himself as a "Household Member." Both share the address in Sullivan.
According to a narrative reported in the documents, Assistant Attorney General Charlie Boyle attempted to dismiss the welfare fraud investigation as not worthy of prosecution during a June 9, 2026 video conference -- just days after Platner became the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/ad11b8db-a4cc-4c24-a3ff-3b65d60e8074?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

According to the memo, a senior fraud investigator reminded Boyle that his argument for dismissing the welfare fraud investigation was, in fact, false.
Boyle then proceeds to tell the fraud investigators that he would grant subpoenas for them, but he'd never prosecute the case "as it was MaineCare only" and "there was no recoupment."
The record suggests that the Attorney General's Office was seeking to downplay or keep quiet a welfare fraud scandal that might embarrass a top Democrat politician.
The probe, handled by Reporting Officer Jodi Look, was still marked "Active" and "Work In Process" as of late 2025 into mid-2026 -- squarely overlapping Platner's public campaign activities.

Graham Platner's household was being investigated for welfare fraud even as Platner dismissed claims of widespread welfare fraud. Jul 8 | | | | | | | | | | | State of Maine welfare fraud investigators have been quietly investigating the wife of disgraced progressive icon and alleged rapist Graham Platner for defrauding the Medicaid program, according to records obtained by The Robinson Report. | | ---|---|--- The documents, provided by a source who asked to remain anonymous, show alleged welfare overpayments totaling more than $9,000 in Medicaid benefits, known in Maine as MaineCare. The records, from a "Fraud Investigation Recovery" case opened under Incident #2511-014, list Amy J. Gertner, Platner's wife, as the suspect and Platner himself as a "Household Member." Both share the address in Sullivan. According to a narrative reported in the documents, Assistant Attorney General Charlie Boyle attempted to dismiss the welfare fraud investigation as not worthy of prosecution during a June 9, 2026 video conference -- just days after Platner became the Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate. | | ---|---|--- Support The Robinson Report today... According to the memo, a senior fraud investigator reminded Boyle that his argument for dismissing the welfare fraud investigation was, in fact, false. Boyle then proceeds to tell the fraud investigators that he would grant subpoenas for them, but he'd never prosecute the case "as it was MaineCare only" and "there was no recoupment." The record suggests that the Attorney General's Office was seeking to downplay or keep quiet a welfare fraud scandal that might embarrass a top Democrat politician. The probe, handled by Reporting Officer Jodi Look, was still marked "Active" and "Work In Process" as of late 2025 into mid-2026 -- squarely overlapping Platner's public campaign activities. ? clean_body: | Friend, For far too long, the political establishment has told us what’s not possible in Tennessee. They’ve told us to lower our expectations, accept uninspired agendas, and sit quietly while politicians like Marsha Blackburn drain our communities and put corporate donors ahead of everyday families. They want us to believe this state can't change, that in fact, being great means going backward. But Tennesseans know better, and while politicians like Marsha Blackburn spend their days avoiding accountability and hiding from constituents and reporters ,we’ve been building a movement— door by door, call by call, text by text, county by county. This campaign is proudly fueled by grassroots volunteers and donors , working-class families, and good old-fashioned elbow grease. No corporate PACS, no backroom deals , just you. From small towns to big cities, we are building a multiracial, multigenerational movement of real Tennesseans—ranchers and retail workers, teachers and neighbors, students and retirees, coming together to build something new. Look around. People are seeing themselves in this campaign because we all want the same thing: a government thatreturns results for Tennesseans based on common sense, compassion, and courage. Let's be clear:flipping Tennessee is hard. But hard is not impossible. Victory is within our reach , but it only happens when we all roll up our sleeves and do our own small part. We cannot wait for someone else to step up. Early voting begins on July 17. The countdown is officially on, and we need a collective push right now that cannot be denied. | | DO YOUR PART: Here are a few of the crucial events happening across the state over just the next few days. Find an opportunity below, plug in, and let's get to work : TODAY(Wednesday, July 8th) @ 6:00 PM CST / 7:00 PM EST – Text Bank to GOTV: Prefer texting? Help us reach voters directly from your phone. Training provided. Thursday , July 9th @ 5:00 PM – Memphis Sign Waving: Meet Team Green at the intersection of Union Ave and Cooper in Memphis. Wave signs, spread the word, and take a yard sign home with you. Thursday , July 9th @ 5:00 PM CST – Phone Bank to GOTV: Another chance to jump on the phones and talk to voters before early voting starts. This Saturday – Statewide Canvass Launches: We are launching simultaneous door-knocking operations this Saturday in Memphis , Nashville, and Chattanooga to power our final stretch. Jerri will be there at the Nashville launch to fire up the crowd before we hit the pavement! No experience is necessary—we’ll provide the training, materials, and pair you with an experienced canvasser. Just bring a charged phone, comfortable walking shoes, and water. We all have a part to play in this fight. Whether you can give one shift or every weekend, your time, your work, and your support matters. If you can't make it to an event,= If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | = = | = = | = = Don't sit this one out. Let's build this movement together. Onward, Jerri Green Democratic Candidate for Tennessee Governor greenforgovernor.com Green For Governor P.O. Republicans’ access to megadonors and over $100 million from the RNC and NRSC gives Republicans a major cash advantage, and MAGA knows it. They've been stockpiling cash for months in preparation for this decision. Huffpost: Jeanine Pirro’s Cases Keep Falling Apart, And The Judges Have Had Enough [https://prod.cdn.everyaction.com/images/van/EA/EA007/1/89215/images/Huffpost_PirroDC.png]
Former Fox News host Jeanine Pirro was sworn in as the U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia last year. The position of US Attorney for DC is important because it serves as both the federal prosecutor and the local district attorney in the nation's capital, often handling some of the most impactful cases across the country.
Pirro's qualifications for the job -- aside from serving as the elected district attorney for Westchester County in New York decades ago -- appeared to be her unwavering support of Donald Trump on TV and his claims about the 2020 election, which she repeated on air and was named a defendant in the cases Fox News settled with Dominion Voting Systems.
Now that she's in office, Pirro has seen a historically bad run of casework, including the felony assault charges she brought against a man who threw a sandwich at a Customs & Border Patrol agent who was part of Trump's DC takeover. A grand jury refused to indict him, and it's one of several examples of Pirro's office filing made-for-TV charges that have been thrown out.
We want to hear from voters in your area about her appointment. Will you take our one-click poll right away?

##### _-- Cliff_
_**by David Shuster**_
For more than twenty years, Vladimir Putin and his Kremlin have cultivated the image of Russia as an unstoppable superpower, a nation of inexhaustible military prowess, inexorable political will, and limitless strategic cunning. Western commentators often repeated the myth, showering Putin with adjectives like "formidable," "fearsome," and "unbeatable."
**Then came Ukraine.**
Putin initially promoted the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine as a brief excursion. He called it "a special military operation" and "brisk campaign" to remind an unruly neighbor of its proper place in history.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/744ac40c-5952-4430-8359-e939706ec060?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
At the beginning, even the U.S. State Department thought Zelensky's Ukrainian forces would crumble, the government in Kyiv would evaporate, and Europe would rediscover its habit of accommodating Russian demands.
Instead, the invaders encountered an unpleasant reality. Nations, like individuals, occasionally refuse to cooperate with the stories written about them.
The war has now become an exhibition not of Russian omnipotence but of Ukrainian ingenuity. Possessing fewer aircraft, fewer ships, fewer tanks, and fewer men, Ukraine has repeatedly accomplished what military orthodoxy insisted could not be done.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/744ac40c-5952-4430-8359-e939706ec060?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Ukraine has transformed inexpensive drones into strategic weapons, converted technological imagination into battlefield leverage, and compelled a vastly larger adversary to defend territory once presumed safely beyond the reach of war.
This week, Ukraine carried out its longest strike of the war, sending drones some 3,000 kilometers from Ukraine to Russia's largest oil refinery in Omsk and setting it on fire. Omsk is in southern Siberia. It was the first time the war had ever reached the facility, and satellite imagery confirmed direct hits on its most critical refining units.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/744ac40c-5952-4430-8359-e939706ec060?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This successful strike, like other Ukrainian attacks on military facilities, logistics hubs, or energy infrastructure inside Russia carries significance far beyond the immediate damage. It underscores that distance no longer guarantees security. It reminds every Russian citizen that geography no longer provides immunity from the consequences of Putin's warmongering.

There’s no sugarcoating it: Donald Trump fired all 22 members of the National Science Board.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260708-fires-rs [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260708-fires-rs]
FIGHT BACK [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260708-fires-rs]
This is the governing body overseeing the National Science Foundation, one of the most important scientific institutions in the United States — and he fired all of them. At once.
The National Science Board exists for a reason. It oversees billions in federal research funding, advises Congress on science policy, and helps ensure taxpayer dollars support real, evidence-based innovation.
Now that independence is being stripped away.
Let me say this clearly: When political leaders start dismantling independent science institutions, it doesn’t just hurt scientists. It hurts all of us — because that means fewer medical breakthroughs, less climate research, slower progress on cancer treatments, degraded pandemic preparedness, and more.
As a microbiologist and educator, take it from me: Science only works when it is allowed to be independent, transparent, and guided by evidence — not politics.
But what we’re seeing now is a systematic effort to replace expertise with loyalty, and it’s happening at the highest levels of government.
This is exactly why I’m running for Congress. Because we need leaders who will defend science and protect vital institutions like the NSF.
But I can’t take on that fight alone. We’re heading into a critical stretch of this campaign, and we need the resources to compete against entrenched interests that are perfectly comfortable ignoring science. So I’m asking you: Can you chip in $10 or whatever you can today to help me fight for science, facts, and the future of research in America? DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/jc_dsg-em?refcode=260708-fires-rs]
When we let science lead, people thrive. Let’s put facts back in charge — and build a Congress that reflects reason, reality, and hope.
Thank you,

Because of your support, I will officially be facing Greg Abbott this November in the race for Governor of Texas.** Now the real work begins. Over the next five months, my team and I will travel across Texas to share our message, talk with voters about what is at stake, and build the kind of campaign that can win. That means scaling up our field program, hiring staff, and getting our message on TV and online so Texans hear the truth, not Abbott’s lies. And if there’s anything this primary election showed us, it’s that Texans are already showing up. More Democrats voted than Republicans in the primary, and turnout was higher than it has been in years. Texans are paying attention, and they’re ready for a governor with integrity who works for them, not against them. But we can’t take anything for granted. |
Peter,
Everyone should be breathing a sigh of relief about something that just happened in Wisconsin--and then worrying about what could happen in other swing states.
A MAGA activist sued to obtain the private records of thousands of voters in a meritless fishing expedition to find deceased and ineligible people they claimed might still be registered to vote.
Granting MAGA's request would have immediately exposed untold thousands, if not millions, of Wisconsin voters' personal information including addresses and given MAGA ammunition to manipulate or falsify the data and scream that Democrats were committing election fraud.
Thankfully, the Wisconsin Supreme Court with its newly-won liberal majority shot this down. The ruling was 5-2, with all four liberal justices joined by only one lone conservative justice.
This is the danger that Democrats have finally started confronting: neglecting state level races, and surrendering crucial judicial races and State Supreme Court elections, puts in jeopardy all of the effort that goes into winning elections.

subject: Property Taxes can't continue like this.
disclaimer_text: PAID FOR BY KAREN CRNKOVICH FOR JOHNSON COUNTY COMMISSION * 6709 West 119th Street * Ste
body:
Here's my plan to cut waste, control spending, and provide meaningful relief.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | |
Friend,
Every time I knock on a door, I hear the same concern.
Property taxes have become unaffordable.
Families on fixed incomes worry they'll be taxed out of the homes they've spent decades paying for. Young families are finding it harder to buy their first home. Even renters are paying more because landlords pass higher property taxes along through higher rent.
_It doesn't have to be this way._
Over the last several years, Johnson County's budget has skyrocketed. In the past five years it has increased nearly 50%. This has added hundreds of millions of dollars in spending while staffing has grown far faster than our population. At the same time, homeowners have watched their property tax bills climb year after year.
Government should live within its means just like every family and every business has to.
As a business owner, I've balanced budgets, controlled costs, made payroll, and found ways to do more with less. Those aren't political talking points. They're responsibilities I've lived with every day.
As your County Chair, I will make property tax relief my top priority by:
* Right-sizing reserves. The county has a policy, we should follow it.
* Conducting a top-to-bottom review of county spending to eliminate waste and duplication.
* Challenging every department to justify new spending before asking taxpayers for more.
* Returning the government to its core responsibilities instead of funding pet projects and personal agendas, like Mike Kelly does.
* Measuring every program by results and data, not intentions.

Johnson County doesn't have a revenue problem. It has a spending problem.
We can protect our AAA bond rating, maintain excellent public safety and county services, invest wisely in our future, and still provide meaningful property tax relief. It simply requires leadership that is willing to ask tough questions and make responsible decisions.
I'm running because I believe Johnson County can remain the best place in America to live, work, and raise a family without pricing people out of their homes.
If you agree it's time for a new direction, I'd be honored to earn your vote and your support.
Please consider joining me in this fight by contributing $25, $50, $200, or any amount you are able.

A year and a half after the historic fires in Southern California, wildfires are becoming more frequent and more devastating. This is no longer a seasonal, summertime issue – it has a year-round impact that requires preparation and federal support.

Before Congress, I co-founded an organization to stop the wildfire crisis. It continues to be a cornerstone of my work in Washington.

Wildfires affect our communities, our economy, and our national security. I'm leading the charge in Congress to strengthen prevention, innovation, and education.

It's why I'm introducing new legislation, the bipartisan Wildfire Response Modernization Act, to strengthen the wildfire monitoring program we rely on – earlier detection, faster evacuations, and safer conditions for firefighters.

Friends,
Since 2024, California has become safer from gun violence than any other time on record — proving that a comprehensive, data-driven approach can transform public safety.
But now, we find ourselves at a dangerous crossroads. While we are working towards a solution, the Trump administration is running from its responsibility to do the same — gutting investments in violence prevention, law enforcement, and victim care.
That’s why I’m proud to announce that this week, we released the final part of our strategic plan to sustain California’s record against gun violence.
This report includes more than 70 recommendations for policymakers and stakeholders across the state to strengthen investments and unite multiple systems around a coordinated plan for prevention, protection, and accountability.
While the Trump administration guts gun violence prevention funding, we are building an effective blueprint for public safety.
Our progress has been transformational.
As recently as 2010, a child under 18 was more likely to die from bullet wounds in California than in the rest of the U.S. on average. By 2024, that trend had reversed, and a child in California was less likely to die from bullet wounds than a child elsewhere.
This progress was not an accident. It was the result of a sustained commitment to gun violence prevention policies and investments.
We cannot afford to lose that momentum now.
Our mission is clear: prevent gun violence, protect lives, and ensure every Californian can feel safe in their home and community. If you agree, add your name to show your support today → [https://secure.ngpvan.com/VnM2QDCxTke_MAzCHw7SNg2]
ADD MY NAME [https://secure.ngpvan.com/VnM2QDCxTke_MAzCHw7SNg2]
Gun violence is a public health crisis, and as your Attorney General, I am committed to using every single tool at our disposal to solve it.
Thank you for being a part of this important work.
In solidarity,
Rob

You'd think after wasting millions of taxpayer dollars on a project that literally started falling apart, the Trump Administration would try something different.
Instead, they're doubling down.
The Interior Secretary just announced that the SAME company awarded a $14.6 million no-bid contract to repaint the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool will now be hired to repair the damage to its own work.

Read that again: The same contractor. The same failed project. More taxpayer dollars. And no accountability.
This is exactly why I launched an Oversight Committee investigation into the Reflecting Pool fiasco.
The costs ballooned from what Donald Trump publicly claimed would be around $2 million to nearly $15 million.
The paint peeled. The water turned green with algae. Millions more dollars were spent trying to fix the problems. And now the administration wants to reward the same contractor with even more work.
That's not how government is supposed to operate.
When ordinary Americans make a mistake at work, they're expected to fix it. When politically connected contractors fail under Donald Trump, they get another contract.
That's not accountability. That's corruption. And as Ranking Member of the House Oversight Committee, I'm demanding answers — because the American people deserve to know why they are once again being asked to foot the bill for Trump’s sweetheart deals.

subject: The Supreme Court took a sledgehammer to our rights.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Elect Evan Hunt
body:
Anti-corruption movements like ours can fight back. | | [ ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.XaF8mXqsA6b2dSPmhsleMYE5U9NTRbOMLNsSMiwuHsSkvWspXpNzcqkzSIoupdDWkL2pjwIimGUsMZ1ZguqiawQwc8Iht3aCrkdXpsjBpSLw1ZyD5bxKE_JcgYrCqbqGL4A4GOaM6_QBZE6IxR7YVJQ8qb0wyYSznc1lOsjYYEKjkTr7D9PhkgB7Gm8qP23j_ySQ9u5IK9d2H3UN9hnxnlI1Qnqq0jVw7DjVOgR-RN_9Kz-4VkNqgqhrprDO94wd6H3KKSUo4h0jMNLsL5qE3n8aDjv12gXOhXJ-PcvP1S3S1c-p76Cg04ZjrTFVKNSh/4s5/tnPfZe_CQIS9gF8YLNvNdA/h0/h001.-rni_trZOPQ9pNRfutgVKvt80NR0j3-2KAJUBZe74fI)
---
Peter, The Supreme Court just wrapped up its term by taking a sledgehammer to a whole set of rights we have been fighting to protect. The last three rulings in particular tell us the dangerous future this captured Court is trying to take the country - and demonstrate perfectly why **we are long overdue for a code of ethics and term limits for the Supreme Court.**
---
[ **REFORM THE COURT** ](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt890FVuYJPi7ocBH1hdaNG33UpSmCzn7kJ2iy3zam-3xsFoWllbyoBqDYWNrhth6OHcrq5Fq5kCjJqr_um5xBUdxHlga9738njKJszG97OOhOM271Ay3s6cFwJsh7VMvCAIUG18f4npTxRqXb9iDeE0V5wMB7y4kOTkTP-mPV4vsZ5pJjmEaer0foyXsNcoVfRxDW5iR8DPX146KgnN0K0bX36K-YXnp1MethgRz_u_89aoGrMyzg_7AcV8PpG7sMiG7y80VBU1o9TDfiG5RX9fFV1SMQYUJtbsfF__PIAma6V2DyGUaPO5A1T7BmVd95zht88pCWLx3K1wAwkfQpKNU/4s5/tnPfZe_CQIS9gF8YLNvNdA/h1/h001.Lsljs_YarNSbj7b4PBkFLdZu864a7PpIycxDieu-goA)
---
_Let 's break down last week's major decisions._ First, the money. The Court struck down limits on how much political parties can spend in coordination with their candidates. In simple terms, **the billionaires and dark money groups who already had the loudest voice in our politics just got a bullhorn.** Then came the cases that got labeled as being about transgender athletes in sports. But the reasoning the Court used reaches far beyond sports. To rule the way they did, the justices had to weaken the legal standard that stops the government from treating people differently based on who they are. That same standard is what protects women from being paid less for the same work, what protects people of faith from being singled out, and what protects any of us from a government that decides one group deserves fewer rights than another. **When you undermine the rights of one group, you open that threat for everyone.** [**I 'm running for Congress to stand up for EVERY SINGLE person in this district. Will you pitch in $25, $50, $100 or more today to help me flip TX-03 and rein in this corrupt court?**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfqs6gc2C5hUDUAX_oNaSPVDobFeqfVfzIW2x4J26hzyt890FVuYJPi7ocBH1hdaNG33VD5A9m9Om3BlE38k688kA9KmyT8ObL2x7P7YvzgCGwgg7aAiRU2FVPJ9Yh6611_aij-8pTd-Hw1N2MjElr5-IgIiONKAESOKLaz3OTZFoP0SSIkm__M_sAChuxyfNjW_KMj9RGjKDYgXX4SkK2oPVt2J7heAiAtt9JAgLhvHCPJxajFRMtIc3X7C_sgSgAtr2wF8xSisjktf7ZyguxPzxAW4jx1g9M_x0ruEsaLEWoPzwxhj1IqBIKerKpniIcEWGJ42tYjnysKy6UXRgTcptimmUgVoj9VzHnXaVGCofdlbI-5y-zvT5JlhcSd77WCs/4s5/tnPfZe_CQIS9gF8YLNvNdA/h2/h001.g-Zh5w2R12nySpvNH4w7qSFH-m7wDkwN63eQnjMyFZY) And then there was birthright citizenship. The good news is the Court upheld it. The gut-check is that the constitutional promise that every child born here is an American, survived by a single vote. **And MAGA forces are already circling for a retirement on that bench so they can install one more loyalist and finish the job next time.** Birthright citizenship helped us become the most dynamic and innovative country on Earth because we welcomed the world's talent instead of fearing it. Unlike Keith Self's rampant bigotry and anti-immigrant fear-mongering, this is a movement that believes you don't mess with the American melting pot. clean_body: Anti-corruption movements like ours can fight back. | | Peter, The Supreme Court just wrapped up its term by taking a sledgehammer to a whole set of rights we have been fighting to protect. The last three rulings in particular tell us the dangerous future this captured Court is trying to take the country - and demonstrate perfectly why we are long overdue for a code of ethics and term limits for the Supreme Court. Let 's break down last week's major decisions. First, the money. The Court struck down limits on how much political parties can spend in coordination with their candidates. In simple terms, the billionaires and dark money groups who already had the loudest voice in our politics just got a bullhorn. Then came the cases that got labeled as being about transgender athletes in sports. But the reasoning the Court used reaches far beyond sports. To rule the way they did, the justices had to weaken the legal standard that stops the government from treating people differently based on who they are. That same standard is what protects women from being paid less for the same work, what protects people of faith from being singled out, and what protects any of us from a government that decides one group deserves fewer rights than another. When you undermine the rights of one group, you open that threat for everyone. And then there was birthright citizenship. The good news is the Court upheld it. The gut-check is that the constitutional promise that every child born here is an American, survived by a single vote. And MAGA forces are already circling for a retirement on that bench so they can install one more loyalist and finish the job next time. Birthright citizenship helped us become the most dynamic and innovative country on Earth because we welcomed the world's talent instead of fearing it. Unlike Keith Self's rampant bigotry and anti-immigrant fear-mongering, this is a movement that believes you don't mess with the American melting pot. This is exactly why I am proud to be a Take BAC Congress candidate. A Court this captured by money and ideology is proof that we need lasting reform: term limits, a binding ethics code for the justices, an end to congressional stock trading, and getting the flood of dark money out of our politics for good. subject: A year of blank checks. A year of fighting back.

No oversight.1 And while billions flowed to turbocharge detention and deportation, this administration slashed over $1 trillion from healthcare and food assistance — the very programs working families depend on to survive.2 Behind every one of these numbers is a household like the ones in our community — a citizen kid at the dinner table, a parent who didn’t come home, a family holding its breath. **[United We Dream is on the frontlines organizing to protect all working people, including immigrants. I have an alarming update--and it couldn't come at a worse time.
Republicans just surpassed Democrats in registered voters in Louisiana for the first time in the state's 214 year history.
---
| | [](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FxmQrNi6eoQ3m-BTuzcFZ-jXqUEUTTgg-FnE01V-z8LUPUiVcnM3eCWAFhA_5Tu8QeqbUz6WUCBENFEBGBFBVQddYded44FtoraGF4gRqQ7UrQLmGUIHIDtCcKkhlXVgnMxnYBi0cMdbCXURzXbq2LqYvsuNUyGLYnTKOcg3ZFXelm69t0cjM4Kl7Tgx-evK8gEjolMIckckaLDWiKPSTyior6Gi4ajn&c=K7kT7w9zw27DRSc-5DtYObXCfdCsqCKy9Mgry9c6bMrwM53JMWurBQ==&ch=cEwoI5VSLXEppxZ6t9Yqf2eIwdu_vzTFpYR_PRvWCSDKsrE219p8lg==)

I am not going to lie to you--this is very troubling news. Our voter registration lead has allowed us to win statewide as recently as 2019, when we reelected Democrat John Bel Edwards as governor for a second consecutive term.
And Louisiana has a major U.S. Senate race this November. The Democrat nominee, Jamie Davis, has a real opportunity to pull off a shocking upset and flip LA's senate seat--a win that would all but guarantee Democrats retake the Senate in November.
Due to the backlash against MAGA and the strength of Jamie's campaign, legendary Democratic strategist James Carville has said he believes Democrats have a real "fighting chance" to win this race.
But with Republicans taking the voter registration lead, our ability to win statewide is now in serious jeopardy.
That's why we're launching an emergency initiative to regain the voter registration lead. Starting this month, our No More Silence - Roll to the Polls Tour will see us visit 14 cities across 7 regions with a goal to register 50,000 new voters, recruit No Party voters, and make sure every voter in Louisiana knows how, when, and where to cast a ballot.
The midterm elections are in just 118 days. That's not a lot of time and it's going to take some major resources to regain our voter registration lead.
[That's why we're asking Democrats across the country to pitch in today: Can I count on you to rush a donation of $50, $25, or whatever you can spare to help the Louisiana Democrats register voters, retake the lead, and flip the U.S, Senate blue?](https://wkfbo8hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001FxmQrNi6eoQ3m-BTuzcFZ-jXqUEUTTgg-FnE01V-z8LUPUiVcnM3eCWAFhA_5Tu8bRtSE2gUGJC2G1zm9H5vxWtTMkx3J30TLl8QE38vHMfo2tZ_JAgn9QcCurwERXRcsdQQ5jEE8MQaa86fWJskdiDhfSn4DsMxZZ_tHHJvI5Tqx249EWfzJau5jtBPd5lvhfUYixemoZ_6gWK7eNGBUIxGY7oz5CmCKKXcJGGbsk8=&c=K7kT7w9zw27DRSc-5DtYObXCfdCsqCKy9Mgry9c6bMrwM53JMWurBQ==&ch=cEwoI5VSLXEppxZ6t9Yqf2eIwdu_vzTFpYR_PRvWCSDKsrE219p8lg==)

Republicans just surpassed Democrats in registered voters in Louisiana for the first time in the state's 214 year history. | | == I am not going to lie to you--this is very troubling news. Our voter registration lead has allowed us to win statewide as recently as 2019, when we reelected Democrat John Bel Edwards as governor for a second consecutive term. And Louisiana has a major U.S. Senate race this November. The Democrat nominee, Jamie Davis, has a real opportunity to pull off a shocking upset and flip LA's senate seat--a win that would all but guarantee Democrats retake the Senate in November. Due to the backlash against MAGA and the strength of Jamie's campaign, legendary Democratic strategist James Carville has said he believes Democrats have a real "fighting chance" to win this race. But with Republicans taking the voter registration lead, our ability to win statewide is now in serious jeopardy. That's why we're launching an emergency initiative to regain the voter registration lead. Starting this month, our No More Silence - Roll to the Polls Tour will see us visit 14 cities across 7 regions with a goal to register 50,000 new voters, recruit No Party voters, and make sure every voter in Louisiana knows how, when, and where to cast a ballot. body:
Let’s be clear about what’s at stake

| | | | | | This is JD Vance. I have an important message for you to read today. Just hear me out.
Peter, we are staring down the most important midterm election of our lives.
If we lose our razor-thin House majority in November, Democrats will incinerate the America First agenda, and everything that we have fought so hard to accomplish will be for nothing. We have so much more work to do, but we simply cannot deliver on our goals if we don't defend our majority right now.
[The future of the America First agenda and of our country depends on what happens this November.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNzA4X0xLLUZWLjExMDExN190MTk1MTM5Ny0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDcwOF9MSy1GVi4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NTEzOTctMjA2OCJ9/CkQjqs1ccGb76sgJny8Myw)
The road to keeping our majority runs straight through Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District, because it is exactly the kind of razor-thin, competitive battleground that will decide control of the House.
If we want to hold the line and protect our progress, we must stand behind strong conservative leaders like Jen Kiggans. If we can’t defend critical seats like hers, we won't have the numbers we need to save our country and deliver on our promises.

If the Left takes back power, here is what it looks like:
* Open Borders: They will immediately stall our successful efforts to secure the southern border.
* Economic Chaos: They will push for massive tax hikes and reckless spending, hurting working families.
* Endless Roadblocks: They will use their new power to launch endless partisan investigations and block the America First agenda at every turn.

We cannot afford to give them the power to derail all the progress we've fought so hard to achieve.
Jen Kiggans is exactly the kind of leader we need in Washington: a Navy veteran, a Nurse Practitioner, and a conservative powerhouse leader who knows how to get things done.

They’re getting ready to dump millions of dollars of dark money into VA-02 with one clear goal: flip this seat blue, seize the Speaker's gavel, and destroy our momentum.](https://trk.join.jenforcongress._cmVjdXJyaW5nPXRydWUmZXhfdGlkPTIwMjYwNzA4X0xLLUZWLjExMDExN190MTk1MTM5Ny0yMDY4JnV0bV9jYW1wYWlnbj0yMDI2MDcwOF9MSy1GVi4xMTAxMTdfdDE5NTEzOTctMjA2OCJ9/rXdjDPGs28T2Il4cSrOylA)

clean_body: Let’s be clear about what’s at stake | | | | | | This is JD Vance. I have an important message for you to read today. Just hear me out. Peter, we are staring down the most important midterm election of our lives. If we lose our razor-thin House majority in November, Democrats will incinerate the America First agenda, and everything that we have fought so hard to accomplish will be for nothing. We have so much more work to do, but we simply cannot deliver on our goals if we don't defend our majority right now. The road to keeping our majority runs straight through Virginia’s 2nd Congressional District, because it is exactly the kind of razor-thin, competitive battleground that will decide control of the House. If we want to hold the line and protect our progress, we must stand behind strong conservative leaders like Jen Kiggans. If we can’t defend critical seats like hers, we won't have the numbers we need to save our country and deliver on our promises. | | Let’s be exceedingly clear about what’s at stake: If we lose the House, the consequences for our movement will be devastating. Hakeem Jeffries and the far-Left radicals will take the Speaker's gavel, instantly grinding our momentum to a halt. If the Left takes back power, here is what it looks like: Open Borders: They will immediately stall our successful efforts to secure the southern border. Economic Chaos: They will push for massive tax hikes and reckless spending, hurting working families. * Endless Roadblocks: They will use their new power to launch endless partisan investigations and block the America First agenda at every turn. We cannot afford to give them the power to derail all the progress we've fought so hard to achieve. Jen Kiggans is exactly the kind of leader we need in Washington: a Navy veteran, a Nurse Practitioner, and a conservative powerhouse leader who knows how to get things done. We can't let them erase our progress. We need to match their firepower right now, protect Jen from the incoming wave of attack ads, and make sure we keep a House Majority that actually fights for everyday Americans. I am asking you today to step up and pitch in. | Hi Peter,

I have three daughters. Like any parent, I think about the kind of place they'll want to build their lives.

_I like to think they’ll stay in Virginia._
---
[](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134885821/632474434/-1785190938?refcode=BLU_EM_UFVF_2026-07-08_1&amount=25&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMjQvMS8xMDM4NTgiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDU5MTNhYzMtZjQ3YS1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=yCXmxsAK6WEf5B-2LgDjO3DOy84qmyANCodFHHOXEsc=)
That's not just a personal hope. It's the reason I ran for Governor.

**Because the truth is, a Commonwealth that works for my daughters only works if it works for everyone.** That means good schools in every zip code. It means housing that working families can actually afford. It means safe neighborhoods, good jobs, and a government that shows up for people instead of getting in their way.

Since January, we have been building exactly that.

We signed paid sick leave into law, so no worker has to choose between their health and their paycheck. We capped insulin costs at $35 a month. We passed meaningful gun safety legislation. We protected reproductive rights. We have taken on energy costs.

None of it happened by accident. All of it took work.

Patriot,

It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners.

But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers...

**Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life.**

They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm.

Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions.

_And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. _

So what comes next for J6ers?

There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do.

[Patriot, as a personal favor to me, can you please send an urgent donation of $10 or more? clean_body: It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. Patriot, It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners. But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers... Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life. They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. So what comes next for J6ers? There are nearly 1,600 Americans who need to rebuild their lives. That's exactly what Stand in the Gap Foundation is helping them do. Stand in the Gap Foundation originally started to help reunite families with a loved one incarcerated due to J6. Now, our focus is on helping those J6ers navigate the challenging process of re-entry into society after being incarcerated. We are committed to providing comprehensive, practical support to ensure that each individual can rebuild their life with dignity, hope, and purpose. DEAR FRIENDS,

Our campaign is ramping up fast, and I'm excited to share the great progress we're making together. Signature collection is going
strong, and we're getting closer every day to getting on the ballot. If you haven't signed yet, please stop by our headquarters in
Warwick 205 Buttonwoods Ave, Warwick, RI.

Last week we had an incredible cookout in Bristol for veterans and community members. Live music, great food, and my wife and kids
were right there with me. It was a wonderful day talking with so many good, hardworking people who love this state and this
country. The Vic Mellor campaign marched in the Ancient and Horribles parade, and the crowd was incredible, full of energy and
patriotism.

As we head deeper into summer, we're ramping up even more. We'll be visiting small businesses across the district, listening to
owners about the real challenges they face and the successes they're fighting for. Rhode Island has been dead last in too many
categories for far too long. It's time we finally put Rhode Island first by creating an environment where good jobs can grow and
small businesses can thrive again.

July 4th always reminds us how precious our freedom really is. It reminds us that our freedom was never guaranteed — it was
earned, and it must be defended. Benjamin Franklin was asked what kind of government we had created. He answered, "A republic, if
you can keep it." That warning rings true today. We need to rededicate ourselves to the American way of life and the American
Dream, the belief that if you work hard, you can build a better life for yourself and your family.

I am proud to be an American. I am thankful every single day to live in the greatest country the world has ever known. While Seth
Magaziner and his party push an anti-American agenda that teaches our kids to be ashamed of this country, I will always stand up
for the values, the history, and the people that made America exceptional. We will not apologize for loving our flag, our
Constitution, or our freedom.

This campaign is about putting Rhode Island first and fighting for the America we believe in. If you're tired of being last, if
you're tired of politicians who divide us and tear down our country, then join us. Stop by headquarters, sign a petition, grab a
sign, or just come say hello.

Together we're going to bring real change.

God bless you, God bless Rhode Island, and God bless the United States of America.

Sincerely,

Vic Mellor

Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District

clean_body: [] DEAR FRIENDS, Our campaign is ramping up fast, and I'm excited to share the great progress we're making together. Signature collection is going strong, and we're getting closer every day to getting on the ballot. If you haven't signed yet, please stop by our headquarters in Warwick 205 Buttonwoods Ave, Warwick, RI. Last week we had an incredible cookout in Bristol for veterans and community members. Live music, great food, and my wife and kids were right there with me. It was a wonderful day talking with so many good, hardworking people who love this state and this country. The Vic Mellor campaign marched in the Ancient and Horribles parade, and the crowd was incredible, full of energy and patriotism. As we head deeper into summer, we're ramping up even more. We'll be visiting small businesses across the district, listening to owners about the real challenges they face and the successes they're fighting for. Rhode Island has been dead last in too many categories for far too long. It's time we finally put Rhode Island first by creating an environment where good jobs can grow and small businesses can thrive again. July 4th always reminds us how precious our freedom really is. It reminds us that our freedom was never guaranteed — it was earned, and it must be defended. Benjamin Franklin was asked what kind of government we had created. He answered, "A republic, if you can keep it." That warning rings true today. We need to rededicate ourselves to the American way of life and the American Dream, the belief that if you work hard, you can build a better life for yourself and your family. I am proud to be an American. I am thankful every single day to live in the greatest country the world has ever known. While Seth Magaziner and his party push an anti-American agenda that teaches our kids to be ashamed of this country, I will always stand up for the values, the history, and the people that made America exceptional. We will not apologize for loving our flag, our Constitution, or our freedom. This campaign is about putting Rhode Island first and fighting for the America we believe in. If you're tired of being last, if you're tired of politicians who divide us and tear down our country, then join us. Stop by headquarters, sign a petition, grab a sign, or just come say hello. Together we're going to bring real change. God bless you, God bless Rhode Island, and God bless the United States of America. Sincerely, Vic Mellor Candidate for Congress, Rhode Island's 2nd District [] [] [] [] [] [] [] Want to change how you receive these emails?

Peter — Alligator Alcatraz may have closed its doors, but a new _CBS News Miami_ investigation just revealed how much Florida taxpayers are on the hook for, and the numbers aren't pretty. The total cost of building and operating the facility is now estimated at **$1.2 billion.** Keeping a single detainee there ran **$3,571 a day** — about **20 times the national average** of $165 that ICE typically pays. And **nearly 15%** of that spending went to one contract for toilets and waste removal. Meanwhile, a year after opening the camp, the federal government has reimbursed Florida for **less than 5%** of what we're owed. **That means you — _the Florida taxpayer_ — are stuck footing the bill for a billion-dollar political stunt in the middle of the Everglades.** This was my opponent's idea. James Uthmeier pitched Alligator Alcatraz as an "efficient, low-cost opportunity." It turned out to be the single most expensive immigration detention center in American history. That's what happens when an Attorney General cares more about pleasing Donald Trump than protecting the people paying the bills. **[As your next Attorney General, I'll investigate every no-bid contract and every dollar wasted on this scheme. | | I am proud to be endorsed by IAM District 751, a union that has spent generations fighting for skilled workers across Northwest Washington, including many at Boeing, the region's largest employer. [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134887129/632478741/1596212816?refcode=2026-07-08-endorsementiam751&recurring=&amount=7&amounts=10,30,50,100,200&refcode2=6ecb386e-f77a-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTMvMS84NzY1OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2ZWNiMzg2ZS1mNzdhLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=LkjapFjyXYjtmeqjMrxTDPiypKEFVAA7NdX_v0g0hgU=)The Pacific Northwest is the aerospace capital of the world, and I am committed to ensuring the United States invests in our aviation future. Aviation manufacturing and maintenance are powerful economic engines, and mean jobs in Northwest Washington. I will continue to support the growth and safety of our country's aviation industry. You cannot have a big league economy with a little league infrastructure. As the top Democrat on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, I have worked hard to bring home federal money and make investments in our roads, bridges, highways and transit to relieve congestion, improve safety and spur economic growth in local communities. Strong infrastructure and a strong aerospace industry go hand in hand. That is why I will continue standing up for families who depend on safe and reliable transportation every day, for communities that depend on infrastructure investments to create jobs, and for an aviation industry that keeps Northwest Washington at the forefront of American manufacturing. When the workers who build the airplanes that fuel our regional economy put their trust in you, it is an honor that carries real meaning. I am grateful to have earned the support of IAM District 751, and I look forward to continuing our work together to strengthen Northwest Washington's economy and create more opportunities for working families. clean_body: IAM District 751 represents the skilled workers across various industries who help power Northwest Washington's economy. | | | | I am proud to be endorsed by IAM District 751, a union that has spent generations fighting for skilled workers across Northwest Washington, including many at Boeing, the region's largest employer. Pacific Northwest is the aerospace capital of the world, and I am committed to ensuring the United States invests in our aviation future. Aviation manufacturing and maintenance are powerful economic engines, and mean jobs in Northwest Washington. I will continue to support the growth and safety of our country's aviation industry. You cannot have a big league economy with a little league infrastructure. As the top Democrat on the Transportation and Infrastructure Committee, I have worked hard to bring home federal money and make investments in our roads, bridges, highways and transit to relieve congestion, improve safety and spur economic growth in local communities. Strong infrastructure and a strong aerospace industry go hand in hand. That is why I will continue standing up for families who depend on safe and reliable transportation every day, for communities that depend on infrastructure investments to create jobs, and for an aviation industry that keeps Northwest Washington at the forefront of American manufacturing. When the workers who build the airplanes that fuel our regional economy put their trust in you, it is an honor that carries real meaning. I am grateful to have earned the support of IAM District 751, and I look forward to continuing our work together to strengthen Northwest Washington's economy and create more opportunities for working families.
