TUBAS, West Bank--Muad Abdelreziq walked slowly through his land on the Al-Forat farm, meandering through rows of banana groves on foot, checking each tree for signs of life. The dead leaves crunched underfoot with each slow, defeated step. No water had reached these groves in five days. "These bananas, they are thirsty," he said. "They are withering away on the ground."
"Everything on the land lives day by day."
Israel had not allowed water to reach 400 dunams (roughly 100 acres) of the farm for five days, Abdelreziq told Drop Site, and what little infrastructure remains is being destroyed. Israeli forces have been rupturing the irrigation pipelines that feed the fields. "I cannot irrigate the herbs, I cannot irrigate the melons," he said. "I cannot replace the water lines. All these families will have nothing. We will have to stop."
Abdelreziq gripped the wheel a little tighter as he drove away from the groves toward the office on the property, glancing at the Israeli military bulldozer just a few feet away that was carving a trench deep into his land. A black military surveillance truck, complete with cameras, antennas, and sensors mounted across its roof, patrolled the site. Stepping into the workers' room, empty chairs lined the walls where employees would take their breaks. Abdelreziq sat and stared at a screen mounted in the corner displaying a live feed of the military construction outside. The Israeli military shot down the last camera he had set up filming the site. He replaced it the next day.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/b816e0d0-ed95-4122-88d4-d3c1dd7db30d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
An Al-Forat employee shows footage of the Israeli military shooting a security camera pointed at the barrier construction site in the occupied West Bank on June 22, 2026. Photo by Wahaj Bani Moufleh.
The 2,000 dunam Al-Forat farm sits in the village of Khirbet Atouf, east of Tubas in the northern Jordan Valley in the occupied West Bank. The farm cultivates bananas, herbs, potatoes, onions, and melons and employs roughly 250 families, supplying markets across the West Bank--land that now sits in the path of a new 22-kilometer separation wall and military road that the army began constructing in March. Israeli settlers have also established a presence on the surrounding land.

The 22-kilometer separation wall and road are part of a much larger Israeli military project dubbed the "Crimson Thread"--a 500-kilometer barrier planned to run along the entire eastern edge of the occupied West Bank, from the southern edge of the occupied Golan Heights in the north to the Red Sea in the south, effectively sealing off the Jordan Valley from the rest of Palestine, according to a leaked Israeli military document signed in August 2025 and first reported by Haaretz in December. The first phase of the project is in the governorate of Tubas. The distance between the wall and an accompanying military road spans 50 meters--a wide path that is carving through some of the most fertile farmland in Palestine. An Israeli army spokesperson told +972 the project was based on "a clear security need, for shaping the terrain and controlling and monitoring vehicular movement."
Maps showing the planned Israeli "Crimson Thread" barrier in the occupied West Bank. Courtesy: Kerem Navot.
Rasheed Khudeiri, a farmer and activist with the Jordan Valley Solidarity Campaign who has spent years documenting settlement expansion in the area, pointed out the hypocrisy of Israel's argument, citing security concerns to displace Palestinians yet allowing Israelis settlers to live in the same area. "How is a closed military firing zone dangerous when they allow settlers who came from Russia or the United States or the Middle East?" Khudeiri told Drop Site. "The owner of the land is not allowed, and the settler is allowed."
Khudeiri says the project will cut from Ain Shibley in the central valley north to the Tayasir military checkpoint, through the communities of Hatu, Ras Al-Ahmar, Anun, and Khirbet Yarza, placing an estimated 180,000 dunams (around 44,000 acres) beyond Palestinian reach.

Tubas Governorate covers 410 square kilometers, 70% of which already falls under Area C--a zone that is under full Israeli security and civil control under the Oslo Accords. There are currently more than nine settlements in the area, seven Israeli military training camps, and more than thirty settlement outposts that have strangled and seized lands in Tubas, nearly reaching the borders of the city of Tubas, according to the mayor, Mahmoud Daraghmeh. "According to their decisions, there is no longer Area A, B, or C," Daraghmeh told Drop Site. "It is all Area C. That is what the Israelis are working toward now."
Khudeiri says the loss will not stay confined to the residents living along the barrier but will have ripple effects that reach into every Palestinian household across the West Bank. The Jordan Valley's fertile soil and warm climate allow farmers to grow vegetables from November through March--winter months when the rest of the West Bank gets colder and produces little to nothing. When farms like Al-Forat stop producing, prices rise across the board. A kilo of cucumbers or tomatoes that cost one shekel to grow locally will cost five or six shekels to import. "Tubas used to be called the breadbasket of Palestine," Daraghmeh said. "Today, it no longer is."

In January, over 100 local residents from Tubas filed a petition to Israel's High Court estimating the direct economic damage from the barrier at $200 million per year. In February, the court issued a temporary injunction halting construction. But on March 3, three days after the U.S. and Israel launched a war on Iran, the military submitted a request for the order to be rescinded--the court agreed, citing undisclosed "security needs." Construction began the following day.
## Settler Attacks
In parallel, settler attacks on farming and Bedouin communities along the planned barrier have surged. At least 117 predominantly Bedouin and herding communities have faced full or partial displacement as a result of settler violence since 2023, [according](https://substack.com/redirect/6c5285b9-7861-4f85-b9fc-53fc3ff49c74?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to Amnesty International, with the northern Jordan Valley bearing the heaviest toll. "Settler violence is not an aberration but an integral part of an organized state policy," Amnesty said. Israeli authorities provided 68 settler herding outposts with 28 million shekels in equipment: ATVs, night vision devices, drones, and generators, according to Peace Now.
"There's a direct, coordinated, organized relationship to support each other," Khudeiri said. "The settlers have direct military support, financial support, every kind of support they want. Even when they attack our villages, the military gives direct support."
Khalid Daraghmeh is 60 years old, and his family had lived in the village of Khirbet Yarza, located east of the city of Tubas, since the Ottoman era. About 100 people lived in the small community, raising livestock, working land they had known for generations. Now, only a handful are left. Settlers began arriving after October 2023, and eventually began staging attacks with increasing levels of violence. They came to the grazing lands first, then to the doorsteps of the community, bringing their own cattle to water from Palestinian wells and graze on Palestinian crops, blocking exits, and making it impossible for families to tend their own land. Children stopped sleeping, Khalid said, and the entire community would freeze at the sight of a tractor.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/3da5d03e-ddc7-4974-9ead-4af396ba7974?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
A shepherd and his son take shade under a tree with their flock in Khirbet Atouf in the occupied West Bank on June 22, 2026. Photo by Wahaj Bani Moufleh.
When the Yarza community called for help, Israeli soldiers did arrive--but not to defend them. "They supported them," Daraghmeh said. "They considered the whole area a military training zone. When we would call because settlers were attacking us, the army would come and protect the settlers."
"[The settlers] kept harassing us, harassing us, harassing us, until they drove us out," Daraghmeh continued. "They started stealing the livestock, stealing everything. They drove us out, and we left."
He and his former neighbors are now scattered across Tubas city, only a few kilometers from their homes, spending money on livestock they can no longer graze and generate little in return.
Meanwhile, Bedouin communities further north in the Jordan Valley have seen some of the worst attacks. In the village of Humsa, 30 masked settlers arrived at a family's home in the middle of the night, beat the entire family, sexually assaulted the father, and stole over 300 sheep, according to the Palestine News Network. Two volunteers from the International Solidarity Movement (ISM) were also beaten and had their passports and phones taken.
An ISM volunteer, who asked not to be named out of fear that Israeli authorities would target them, has spent months doing overnight shifts with families across the valley. Palestinian communities request the volunteers, they said, just so they can sleep with some semblance of protection. "We call it solidarity presence and not protective presence," the volunteer told Drop Site, "because being with the families doesn't actually change much about what happens to the situation. We just serve as witnesses to settler violence or interactions with the military and police."
During one military raid the volunteer witnessed, soldiers conducted violent body searches on the men of a family while a woman collapsed on the floor, unable to breathe. Every time someone moved to help her, a gun was pointed at them and they were told to be silent. "Our presence here really does so little," the volunteer said. "When 30 settlers come and you are two people, there is not very much you can do."
## Redrawing the West Bank
In 2025, the Israeli military launched a massive assault targeting the refugee camps of Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur Shams in the northern West Bank. More than 30,000 Palestinians were displaced in the military operation and have been [unable to return to their homes](https://substack.com/redirect/05a846b4-4a5c-47a6-b0a4-819ed729100a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Now, the focus has shifted to the eastern corridor. When complete, the Crimson Thread project will seal off the West Bank's entire eastern side.
"The Israeli strategy is to divide the towns in the north of the West Bank," Khudeiri told Drop Site. "Tubas divided from Jenin. Nablus divided between Tubas, Nablus, and Jenin. The same with Tulkarm and Qalqilya. This is how they create what they call 'containers.'"
He continued, "Tubas, Nablus, Ramallah, Bethlehem, Silfit--all of these towns, they will be like huge refugee camps without any services, without any rights."
Khudeiri drove through the valley's villages, ending the day in the small village of Bardala where he lives. He was explaining the area's native flora when he abruptly stopped the car. There was a dead bird on the road. He moved it to the side, then stood there for a moment before returning to the car and driving slowly away.

"We belong to this land," Khudeiri said, explaining that he has started keeping some of his knowledge of the area to himself--not writing it down or sharing it publicly, because, he said, whatever Palestinians name and describe can be taken.
"They are trying to steal everything--the name of our plants, the song we use when our people harvest the wheat. We have a lot of things we don't share anymore because they keep stealing more and more."

Without your support, we can 't operate. Please consider becoming a paid subscriber or making a . TUBAS, West Bank--Muad Abdelreziq walked slowly through his land on the Al-Forat farm, meandering through rows of banana groves on foot, checking each tree for signs of life. The dead leaves crunched underfoot with each slow, defeated step. No water had reached these groves in five days. "These bananas, they are thirsty," he said. "They are withering away on the ground." "Everything on the land lives day by day." Israel had not allowed water to reach 400 dunams (roughly 100 acres) of the farm for five days, Abdelreziq told Drop Site, and what little infrastructure remains is being destroyed. Israeli forces have been rupturing the irrigation pipelines that feed the fields. "I cannot irrigate the herbs, I cannot irrigate the melons," he said. "I cannot replace the water lines. All these families will have nothing. We will have to stop." Abdelreziq gripped the wheel a little tighter as he drove away from the groves toward the office on the property, glancing at the Israeli military bulldozer just a few feet away that was carving a trench deep into his land. A black military surveillance truck, complete with cameras, antennas, and sensors mounted across its roof, patrolled the site. Stepping into the workers' room, empty chairs lined the walls where employees would take their breaks. Abdelreziq sat and stared at a screen mounted in the corner displaying a live feed of the military construction outside. The Israeli military shot down the last camera he had set up filming the site. He replaced it the next day. | | ---|---|--- An Al-Forat employee shows footage of the Israeli military shooting a security camera pointed at the barrier construction site in the occupied West Bank on June 22, 2026. Photo by Wahaj Bani Moufleh. The 2,000 dunam Al-Forat farm sits in the village of Khirbet Atouf, east of Tubas in the northern Jordan Valley in the occupied West Bank. The farm cultivates bananas, herbs, potatoes, onions, and melons and employs roughly 250 families, supplying markets across the West Bank--land that now sits in the path of a new 22-kilometer separation wall and military road that the army began constructing in March. Israeli settlers have also established a presence on the surrounding land. The 22-kilometer separation wall and road are part of a much larger Israeli military project dubbed the "Crimson Thread"--a 500-kilometer barrier planned to run along the entire eastern edge of the occupied West Bank, from the southern edge of the occupied Golan Heights in the north to the Red Sea in the south, effectively sealing off the Jordan Valley from the rest of Palestine, according to a leaked Israeli military document signed in August 2025 and first reported by Haaretz in December. The first phase of the project is in the governorate of Tubas. The distance between the wall and an accompanying military road spans 50 meters--a wide path that is carving through some of the most fertile farmland in Palestine. An Israeli army spokesperson told +972 the project was based on "a clear security need, for shaping the terrain and controlling and monitoring vehicular movement." Maps showing the planned Israeli "Crimson Thread" barrier in the occupied West Bank. Courtesy: Kerem Navot. Rasheed Khudeiri, a farmer and activist with the Jordan Valley Solidarity Campaign who has spent years documenting settlement expansion in the area, pointed out the hypocrisy of Israel's argument, citing security concerns to displace Palestinians yet allowing Israelis settlers to live in the same area. "How is a closed military firing zone dangerous when they allow settlers who came from Russia or the United States or the Middle East?" Khudeiri told Drop Site. "The owner of the land is not allowed, and the settler is allowed." Khudeiri says the project will cut from Ain Shibley in the central valley north to the Tayasir military checkpoint, through the communities of Hatu, Ras Al-Ahmar, Anun, and Khirbet Yarza, placing an estimated 180,000 dunams (around 44,000 acres) beyond Palestinian reach. Tubas Governorate covers 410 square kilometers, 70% of which already falls under Area C--a zone that is under full Israeli security and civil control under the Oslo Accords. There are currently more than nine settlements in the area, seven Israeli military training camps, and more than thirty settlement outposts that have strangled and seized lands in Tubas, nearly reaching the borders of the city of Tubas, according to the mayor, Mahmoud Daraghmeh. "According to their decisions, there is no longer Area A, B, or C," Daraghmeh told Drop Site. "It is all Area C. That is what the Israelis are working toward now." Khudeiri says the loss will not stay confined to the residents living along the barrier but will have ripple effects that reach into every Palestinian household across the West Bank. The Jordan Valley's fertile soil and warm climate allow farmers to grow vegetables from November through March--winter months when the rest of the West Bank gets colder and produces little to nothing. When farms like Al-Forat stop producing, prices rise across the board. A kilo of cucumbers or tomatoes that cost one shekel to grow locally will cost five or six shekels to import. "Tubas used to be called the breadbasket of Palestine," Daraghmeh said. "Today, it no longer is." In January, over 100 local residents from Tubas filed a petition to Israel's High Court estimating the direct economic damage from the barrier at $200 million per year. In February, the court issued a temporary injunction halting construction. But on March 3, three days after the U.S. and Israel launched a war on Iran, the military submitted a request for the order to be rescinded--the court agreed, citing undisclosed "security needs." Construction began the following day. Settler Attacks In parallel, settler attacks on farming and Bedouin communities along the planned barrier have surged. At least 117 predominantly Bedouin and herding communities have faced full or partial displacement as a result of settler violence since 2023, to Amnesty International, with the northern Jordan Valley bearing the heaviest toll. "Settler violence is not an aberration but an integral part of an organized state policy," Amnesty said. Israeli authorities provided 68 settler herding outposts with 28 million shekels in equipment: ATVs, night vision devices, drones, and generators, according to Peace Now. "There's a direct, coordinated, organized relationship to support each other," Khudeiri said. "The settlers have direct military support, financial support, every kind of support they want. Even when they attack our villages, the military gives direct support." Khalid Daraghmeh is 60 years old, and his family had lived in the village of Khirbet Yarza, located east of the city of Tubas, since the Ottoman era. About 100 people lived in the small community, raising livestock, working land they had known for generations. Now, only a handful are left. Settlers began arriving after October 2023, and eventually began staging attacks with increasing levels of violence. They came to the grazing lands first, then to the doorsteps of the community, bringing their own cattle to water from Palestinian wells and graze on Palestinian crops, blocking exits, and making it impossible for families to tend their own land. Children stopped sleeping, Khalid said, and the entire community would freeze at the sight of a tractor. | | ---|---|--- A shepherd and his son take shade under a tree with their flock in Khirbet Atouf in the occupied West Bank on June 22, 2026. Photo by Wahaj Bani Moufleh. When the Yarza community called for help, Israeli soldiers did arrive--but not to defend them. "They supported them," Daraghmeh said. "They considered the whole area a military training zone. When we would call because settlers were attacking us, the army would come and protect the settlers." "[The settlers] kept harassing us, harassing us, harassing us, until they drove us out," Daraghmeh continued. "They started stealing the livestock, stealing everything. They drove us out, and we left." He and his former neighbors are now scattered across Tubas city, only a few kilometers from their homes, spending money on livestock they can no longer graze and generate little in return. Meanwhile, Bedouin communities further north in the Jordan Valley have seen some of the worst attacks. In the village of Humsa, 30 masked settlers arrived at a family's home in the middle of the night, beat the entire family, sexually assaulted the father, and stole over 300 sheep, according to the Palestine News Network. Two volunteers from the International Solidarity Movement (ISM) were also beaten and had their passports and phones taken. An ISM volunteer, who asked not to be named out of fear that Israeli authorities would target them, has spent months doing overnight shifts with families across the valley. Palestinian communities request the volunteers, they said, just so they can sleep with some semblance of protection. "We call it solidarity presence and not protective presence," the volunteer told Drop Site, "because being with the families doesn't actually change much about what happens to the situation. We just serve as witnesses to settler violence or interactions with the military and police." During one military raid the volunteer witnessed, soldiers conducted violent body searches on the men of a family while a woman collapsed on the floor, unable to breathe. Every time someone moved to help her, a gun was pointed at them and they were told to be silent. "Our presence here really does so little," the volunteer said. "When 30 settlers come and you are two people, there is not very much you can do." Redrawing the West Bank In 2025, the Israeli military launched a massive assault targeting the refugee camps of Jenin, Tulkarm, and Nur Shams in the northern West Bank. More than 30,000 Palestinians were displaced in the military operation and have been . Now, the focus has shifted to the eastern corridor. When complete, the Crimson Thread project will seal off the West Bank's entire eastern side. "The Israeli strategy is to divide the towns in the north of the West Bank," Khudeiri told Drop Site. "Tubas divided from Jenin. Nablus divided between Tubas, Nablus, and Jenin. The same with Tulkarm and Qalqilya. This is how they create what they call 'containers.'" He continued, "Tubas, Nablus, Ramallah, Bethlehem, Silfit--all of these towns, they will be like huge refugee camps without any services, without any rights." Khudeiri drove through the valley's villages, ending the day in the small village of Bardala where he lives. He was explaining the area's native flora when he abruptly stopped the car. There was a dead bird on the road. He moved it to the side, then stood there for a moment before returning to the car and driving slowly away. "We belong to this land," Khudeiri said, explaining that he has started keeping some of his knowledge of the area to himself--not writing it down or sharing it publicly, because, he said, whatever Palestinians name and describe can be taken. "They are trying to steal everything--the name of our plants, the song we use when our people harvest the wheat. ---

Friends,
Have you seen the latest in Michigan's Senate race? Because this is a big one:
**The Democratic primary for Michigan 's Senate seat just became a two-way race.**
Mallory McMorrow has been an important voice, both in this race and in the State Senate, and for policies that benefit Michigan's children and families. I look forward to working with her in the future to build a stronger Michigan for everyone, and to anyone reading this who was supporting Mallory's inspiring campaign, I invite you to join me in this fight to lower costs, protect manufacturing jobs in Michigan, take on Trump's corruption and abuses of power, and defeat Mike Rogers to flip the Senate blue.
I'm going to be honest with you: this race is really heating up.
There is less than a month to go until the primary - and early voting is just two weeks away.
That means we need all hands on deck from now until Primary Day.
**And now the Senate GOP 's campaign arm is going all in to boost my opponent, and there's one big reason why: Because they know he's their path to flipping Michigan red.**
The fact of the matter is, no one wants Abdul El-Sayed to win more than the GOP. They're betting that he can't beat MAGA Mike Rogers in the general election, so they're willing to spend big money to ensure that he's the nominee.
And you know what, folks? They're right.
Poll after poll shows I'm the ONLY Democrat that has what it takes to defeat Rogers in November and keep Michigan blue.
Because this is about so much more than just one race, one Senate seat, one candidate over another. This is about our country's future, our democracy's future, our families' futures. It's about whether future generations will be able to enjoy the same rights that we do today - that the people who came before us fought so hard for.
With Senate control on the line, we can't take any chances. We need to win the Democratic nomination, and we need to win in November.
**That means we need all hands on deck before polls close on August 4th.**
I'm ready to get to the Senate and keep doing what I've always done for Michiganders: Fight to lower costs, protect manufacturing jobs, and stand up to the far-right's abuses of power.
But the only way for me to do that is if this grassroots movement steps up now to help ensure my team and I have the resources we need to fight back against MAGA's megadonors.
Time is running out and we're going all-out to reach voters in every corner of Michigan, turn out the vote in August, and bring this campaign over the finish line. And, folks, I'll be honest with you: This isn't something I can do alone.
I have a whole team of committed Democrats behind me helping me out every step of the way - and it includes _you._
So I hope you understand that when I ask for your help, it's because you are truly a valued member of this grassroots movement. And if you want to win in Michigan, flip the Senate, and stand up to Trump, this is how we do it.
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/c3bdcc6f-c75d-48a1-a45b-e18738a7ad8b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Thank you.
With grit and determination,
Haley

A personal note from Haley 👋

I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love.

But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican.

I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win.

If you're with me, will you chip in today?

clean_body: We can't afford to take any chances on who we send to the general election | | ---|---|--- | | | Forwarded this email? ? for more We can't afford to take any chances on who we send to the general election | | | Jul 8 | | | | | | Friends, Have you seen the latest in Michigan's Senate race? Because this is a big one: The Democratic primary for Michigan 's Senate seat just became a two-way race. Mallory McMorrow has been an important voice, both in this race and in the State Senate, and for policies that benefit Michigan's children and families. I look forward to working with her in the future to build a stronger Michigan for everyone, and to anyone reading this who was supporting Mallory's inspiring campaign, I invite you to join me in this fight to lower costs, protect manufacturing jobs in Michigan, take on Trump's corruption and abuses of power, and defeat Mike Rogers to flip the Senate blue. I'm going to be honest with you: this race is really heating up. There is less than a month to go until the primary - and early voting is just two weeks away. That means we need all hands on deck from now until Primary Day. And now the Senate GOP 's campaign arm is going all in to boost my opponent, and there's one big reason why: Because they know he's their path to flipping Michigan red. The fact of the matter is, no one wants Abdul El-Sayed to win more than the GOP. They're betting that he can't beat MAGA Mike Rogers in the general election, so they're willing to spend big money to ensure that he's the nominee. And you know what, folks? They're right. Poll after poll shows I'm the ONLY Democrat that has what it takes to defeat Rogers in November and keep Michigan blue. Because this is about so much more than just one race, one Senate seat, one candidate over another. This is about our country's future, our democracy's future, our families' futures. It's about whether future generations will be able to enjoy the same rights that we do today - that the people who came before us fought so hard for. With Senate control on the line, we can't take any chances. We need to win the Democratic nomination, and we need to win in November. That means we need all hands on deck before polls close on August 4th. I'm ready to get to the Senate and keep doing what I've always done for Michiganders: Fight to lower costs, protect manufacturing jobs, and stand up to the far-right's abuses of power. But the only way for me to do that is if this grassroots movement steps up now to help ensure my team and I have the resources we need to fight back against MAGA's megadonors. Time is running out and we're going all-out to reach voters in every corner of Michigan, turn out the vote in August, and bring this campaign over the finish line. And, folks, I'll be honest with you: This isn't something I can do alone. I have a whole team of committed Democrats behind me helping me out every step of the way - and it includes you. So I hope you understand that when I ask for your help, it's because you are truly a valued member of this grassroots movement. And if you want to win in Michigan, flip the Senate, and stand up to Trump, this is how we do it. Thank you. With grit and determination, Haley A personal note from Haley 👋 I'm a lifelong Michigander and the daughter of small-business owners. I've spent my career fighting for Michigan's working families - and now I'm running for the U.S. Senate to keep standing up for the people I love. But here's the truth: Senate control could come down to Michigan. And Trump and his megadonors know it. That's why they're gearing up to spend tens of millions to defeat me and hand this seat to a MAGA Republican. I need your help to fight back. This race will be one of the most competitive - and expensive - in the country, and I'm counting on grassroots support to win. If you're with me, will you chip in today? | | | (C) 2026 Haley for MI 33717 Woodward Ave #539, Birmingham, MI 48009 ? ?

Hey, Angry Democrats.
We are making a brand change.
[Get 30% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/a84e0f60-4bf6-449b-ae25-42f7cc8ce88a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
The Angry Democrat and The Angry Ohioan are now becoming The Angry Democrats and The Angry Ohioans.
That might seem small. It is just an S. But it is bigger than it looks.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/bfa0b8db-cabc-4c2d-b526-c104c2a9398a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Adding the S opens this up. It makes clear that this is not just me. This is not just Matt Diemer sitting here putting out his opinions. This is not one person yelling into the void and hoping somebody hears it.
This is for all Angry Democrats and Angry Ohioans who see what is happening and know something has to change.
It is for people who understand that corruption is not limited to one party. It is for people who are sick of behind-the-scenes deals, hypocrisy, gatekeeping, insider politics, and people in power acting like they are owed our votes, our donations, and our silence.
[Get 30% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/a84e0f60-4bf6-449b-ae25-42f7cc8ce88a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Get 30% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/a84e0f60-4bf6-449b-ae25-42f7cc8ce88a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
This is us saying **We Democrats**. **We Ohioans**.
[Laura Rodriguez-Carbone](https://open.substack.com/users/504723763-laura-rodriguez-carbone?utm_source=mentions) and I have teamed up, and we are opening the door for more people to join us. We are welcoming anyone who wants to be an Angry Democrat or an Angry Ohioan.
Because this was never supposed to be just one voice. It **needs** to be many.
We are putting ourselves out there, and yes, that means we will take the attacks. We will take the criticism. We will be told we do not know our place. We will be told to stay in our lane. We will be told to shut up and vote blue no matter who.
[Get 30% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/a84e0f60-4bf6-449b-ae25-42f7cc8ce88a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We will be told not to criticize our own party. We will be told this is not the time.
But when is the time?
When the party rallies behind horrible candidates with no policies and no vision?
When the average person keeps getting screwed?
When Ohioans are taxed more while their healthcare gets worse, their benefits get whittled away, and their communities get ignored?
When our tax dollars are used for corruption, bribery scandals, billionaire corporations, and sports teams, while infrastructure crumbles and whole neighborhoods are left behind?
When jobs leave, services fail, and the same small group of people keeps making decisions on behalf of everyone else?
And then, after all of that, they still want our donations. They still want our votes. They still want our loyalty.

[Help Fund The Angry Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/5ea771be-133a-42a7-b389-de12ec53b25d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Help Fund The Angry Democrats](https://substack.com/redirect/5ea771be-133a-42a7-b389-de12ec53b25d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
### NO.
That is exactly why the S matters.
The S means this is bigger than one person.
The S means people are allowed to be angry.
The S means Democrats can demand better from Democrats.
The S means Ohioans can demand better from Ohio.
And yes, like the S on Superman's chest, it stands for hope.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/bab368ec-4f9a-4d6f-80de-fe1be9481078?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Not the kind of hope they sell you every election cycle and then forget about when the votes are counted.
Real hope.
The kind that comes from people finally saying enough, stepping forward, and refusing to let the same broken systems keep speaking for them.
The Angry Democrats.
The Angry Ohioans.
That S is important because it reflects all of us.
## Stay Angry.

We need to talk about something that happened a few days ago, because it has implications not just for Brattleboro and the surrounding community, but for all of Vermont. **The board at Brattleboro Memorial Hospital just voted to close their birthing center.** For moms giving birth in that region, there are no close alternatives. That means families facing one of the most important moments of their lives will now have to travel significantly farther to get the care they need. This is heartbreaking. And it is exactly the kind of thing that I’ve been talking about across the state. As our state regulators wrestle with the need to control health care costs, we're going to keep seeing a steady drip of cuts like this one — cuts that may make sense on a balance sheet but are devastating for the communities that depend on these services. **We are scrambling to survive instead of organizing to thrive.** **Vermont needs a multi-year plan that gets health care costs under control while preserving the critical health care services our communities depend on.** That plan has to be built in partnership with those communities, asking what they need, and making sure we deliver it. As your next governor, I promise to be on the ground with you. Not pointing fingers, not issuing statements from a distance — but actually showing up to be part of a solution that works for all Vermonters. What's happening in Brattleboro is a warning for the entire state. Vermont deserves a governor who treats it like one. Aly Richards

Team,
There's a reason _PoliticsPA_ said what's happening in our district could be "an indicator of other fall races."
It's the same reason James Carville said our campaign is "what Democrats need to see."
And it's why **Dan Meuser is polling 17 points below his vote share in 2024.**
The tide is turning in our part of Pennsylvania, and we're meeting the moment.
Our message is resonating because we're focused on the things that actually matter to the people here.

Hi there,

I'm Mai Vang — Sacramento City Councilmember and the Democrat who won first place in the primary for California's 7th Congressional District.

**[In a moment, I'm going to ask you to help power our general election campaign. But first, I want to tell you who I am and why so many people are calling this one of the most important races in the country.](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.iIBo0N5fSFzEFL40Tn-vtbMETCUYClkOrOh9-SNJfquO38L98SklfBdoDq94y0bmNpGkqxcvbwAwPTl2twJS_NE5wKv8qBdSLjoczwyk6r6_NqOIUqrqRvT3YlGUxKUowouXXXrS5T7Sr2Whgpf_h5smODluTdnx3QHlyc-FdNzegLWo65WWNV_atWG4wyW9AZYQOj68wW-Eb2SIBwQZnTQd9p0hawp-B_KaTrUOZ5DQGbkyEt9hFPjqp7Wp29ReUjA9HqGJJ7h2y3n47BD-NJlOoiuhZu73CereaLDs5thj6Ok6nQU0K9HZIAVTk5q8uTUjGL6BEP5YQBGHNU_rhY6kDJa8lz2BdE4HIBqNyg9Yxvo_WXiOQuw1PQ8gFiQ9tIi3HF3iGuOtPLP4eo23NFPMdOTgPk2xvNRlpx8m7XY/4s5/BWDCm6fRQyy46vTIDfnvag/h1/h001.7m2v7f2BBh7yR6lhfh0YcZwtMYd8GkjI8B6sbKVSsWc)**

I'm the daughter of Hmong refugees and the eldest of 16 children, raised in South Sacramento. I know what it means to live paycheck to paycheck, because I've done it my whole life. That's what led me to public service — and it's why I'm running now.
For 20 years, this seat has been held by the same incumbent, and the establishment said it couldn't be challenged. Outspent nearly 3 to 1, we proved them wrong — because voters are ready for a new generation of leadership that actually fights for working people.
**_We can't keep moving at a slow, incremental pace while working families are left behind. We need urgency, and we need clarity:_** **_
_** **_We need Medicare for All — not a system that lets insurance companies decide who gets care._** **_
_** **_We need to abolish ICE — not keep funding an agency that tears families apart._**
We need to end U.S. support for the genocide in Gaza — not send more weapons to continue it.
And we need leaders who answer to people, not corporate PACs. That's why I have never taken a dime from corporate PACs, and I never will.
**[The general election is here, and we're rebuilding from the ground up after spending everything to win the primary. name: Elijah Norton for Arizona Treasurer
subject: The Businessman VS. The Bureaucrat
body:
Real world experience matters.

| | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/1ZpF5TdMRiF?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | |

Dear Peter,
We are now less than two weeks away from the primary election. Throughout this primary, I have focused on educating voters about why I am the best qualified person to serve as your Treasurer. I have not attacked my opponent. Our campaign is working: we have raised nearly twice as much, we’ve traveled to every corner of the state, meeting thousands of voters, and are now polling with a double-digit lead.
However, in recent days, my opponent and her Bush-era consultants have decided to resort to lies, attacks, and negative messaging in a desperate attempt to boost their failing campaign. I know the voters in this election, and I know that they will reject her lies. But for reference, I am sending this e-mail to discuss the facts and the choice you have as a voter (as well as linked sources):
* The state Treasurer manages over $32 billion in assets under management. I believe the Treasurer's office needs someone with real-world experience in business, finance, and investment. **My opponent - who is a career bureaucrat who worked in Congress for John Boehner and Paul Ryan- has never managed a single cent. She has spent her entire life profiting off of taxpayers**. She formed her "business" with [a far-left Democrat](https://us.list-manage.com/nrowyk_h5gj?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b) to create a company that profits from her political connections and public funds; she now considers that her "experience". I consider that corruption and everything wrong with politics today.
* I have REAL experience creating jobs, generating revenue, and investing millions of dollars. As the Executive Chairman and President of a **global** insurance organization, I manage over $100 million in claims reserves and invest them in accordance with conservative investment guidelines. I know how to manage money, make safe, stable returns, and what it takes to invest money on a large scale. My opponent **has never directly invested two nickels, nor has she ever made a direct investment decision.** She uses the term “stewardship” as a cover for mediocrity and for allowing bureaucrats - not the elected Treasurer to oversee Arizona's investments. She**** is grossly underqualified to manage **$32 billion of your dollars. She has never owned a real business and managed "private funds".** Sitting on a 7-member education [board ](https://us.list-manage.com/VsxV7LP2NX5?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b)(whose primary focus is on educator discipline and curriculum development) with a $6 million budget does not qualify someone to manage 32 billion dollars of YOUR money.
* I believe a DOGE-style audit of our state budget isn't just important, **it is necessary.**[**We have had a massive amount of waste, fraud, and abuse in Arizona over the past 20 years**](https://us.list-manage.com/18ziA1t04fi?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b)**** \- some of which the auditor-general has failed to uncover**.** It's time to stop it once and for all. That is why the President of the Arizona Senate, leadership in the Arizona House (including the Chairman of the Audit Committee), and over 20 current and former members of the state legislature have endorsed me. **It's time we audit our state and stop waste, fraud, and abuse once and for all.**
* A disturbing report was published by the Auditor-General in April of 2026. The [report ](https://us.list-manage.com/8ZWo1jeSMBS?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b)found a **$68 million accounting discrepancy** by the Treasurer's office in 2024. When questioned, the Treasurer's office essentially called it a "rounding error". **$68 MILLION DOLLARS OF YOUR MONEY IS NOT A "ROUNDING ERROR". ** Please read the article [_**HERE**_](https://us.list-manage.com/4wCAvY_AI1T?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b) _**.** _I am not running to cover up discrepancies or bureaucratic incompetence - I am running to expose them and be accountable directly to you, the people of Arizona.
* I had the privilege and honor of serving as the Arizona Republican Party Treasurer from 2023 to 2025. During that time, I managed over $20 million worth of funds - **$10 million of which was spent on re-electing President Trump. Over $1 million was spent on keeping our Legislature Republican.** And the rest was spent on making the 2024 cycle one of the most successful in Arizona history **-**[**securing some of the biggest victories in the history of the AZGOP**](https://us.list-manage.com/fUlqqPiYmiR?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b). **I helped save the AZGOP from bankruptcy; had the first CPA audit performed in 10 years for 2022 and 2023; and was honored to receive a Defender of Freedom Award in the January 2026** meeting for my efforts in saving the AZGOP from financial ruin. **At the same time,**[**my opponent was thrown out of the AZGOP meeting**](https://us.list-manage.com/10Zt27kPmL3?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b)**into the cold by armed security guards for stealing money from the State Party - as her first official campaign act. **

Please read the above and realize the difference. Ask yourself this question - **who would you rather manage your retirement account or your child's college fund - a dishonest career bureaucrat who has never invested real money in her life, or a proven business leader who turned a $1,000 investment into a half-a-billion global company.** The choice is simple— and it is up to you.
Find a voting location near you at [my.arizona.vote](https://us.list-manage.com/BYLfKZ7nIUD?e=4bbfddebd7&c2id=3a28d4e25e67509d3bf28128bdefbc4b).
Thank you,
Elijah Norton

Dear Friend,
A few months ago, a man sat across from me and said six words I have not been able to forget: **"The truth is not for sale."** [](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)
**[His name is Dr. Rick Addante.](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.)** He is a neuroscientist. He worked with NASA. And when he came on my podcast, he told the world what he had discovered inside Florida Institute of Technology — **caught on a recording the university never wanted you to see.** [▶ WATCH HIM GET SERVED AND CHIP IN $35](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Here is what Rick exposed: the university president, in a faculty meeting, explaining how the school would keep roughly **$7 million in taxpayer grant money** by changing the words in their documents — so it looked like they were complying with the state's rules when they were not. **"Change some words so they're not being scraped... allows us to do our work."** Not change the conduct. Just change the words, so the public couldn't tell. When our report went out, the president emailed the entire campus and attacked the whistleblower. Days later, Rick was terminated. Then came the offer: **$96,000 to resign quietly, stay silent, and promise never to sue.** **He said no.** A NASA neuroscientist turned down nearly six figures — and is now **mowing his neighbor's lawn for $30 to feed his family** — because he would not put a price on the truth. [▶ WATCH THE JUDGE ORDER HIM TO SURRENDER HIS GUNS](https://link.email.america1stwarroom.) Sarah’s congressional office was just awarded the 2026 Democracy Award for Best Constituent Service in Congress!
# [](https://act.sarahmcbride.com/go/1269?t=1&akid=3512%2E21716%2EC0ee7x)
Exciting news:
**Sarah’s congressional office was just awarded the 2026 Democracy Award for Best Constituent Service in Congress!**
Since she took office last January, Sarah and her team have helped more than **1,500 of our neighbors in Delaware** navigate federal agencies, ultimately returning **$6.5 million** in backlogged benefits.
This work doesn’t always get the most attention, but it’s some of the most important work that happens in Congress.
Behind every single case is a veteran waiting for benefits that they’ve earned, a senior trying to get their Social Security check, a family stuck in passport limbo, or someone simply trying to get a clear answer from their government. And we’re proud that Sarah and her team in Congress have been so effective in helping get those cases resolved.
**That’s what public service is all about.** Not attention seeking, performative stunts designed to help a politician go viral. Just a government that treats people with respect and follows through on its promises.

body:
[1]Justice Democrats

Peter,

AIPAC’s super PAC, United Democracy Project, just dropped more than
$400,000 on ads to protect their stooge, Rep. Wesley Bell, in Missouri’s
1st congressional district.

Their first ad in defense of Bell claims he is leading the fight against
Donald Trump and ICE, but that couldn’t be further from the truth.

[ https://go.justicedemocrats.com/go/140221?c0=jd-em-20260708-1-cb.-EPKkH&refcode=em20260708-38001&amounts=10%2C27%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&amount=10&t=1002&akid=38001%2E1203867%2EEarayt ]Tweet from @AndrewSolender: "United Democracy Project, AIPAC's super
PAC, is running ads in support of Wesley Bell in #MO01 saying he "is
leading the fight to abolish ICE" and "fighting against Trump." Bell is
facing a challenge from former Rep. Cori Bush, who he unseated in 2024.";
a screenshot of Wesley Bell standing in front of a group of people is
attached.

Bell was 1 of 75 House Democrats who voted to "express gratitude" to ICE
for "protecting the homeland."

He’s no progressive, but he and his AIPAC network backers are trying to

Fellow Patriot,

That is why I fight so hard in the Senate. And that is why I am reaching out to you today about a race I believe will shape the future - Montana. This is Katie Britt, Alabama's first elected female Senator. Peter,

It's been over a year since President Trump pardoned us J6 prisoners.

But even with the pardons, you may not realize what life is like for many J6ers...

**Some are homeless to this day. Some can 't get a job because of the time they've spent in jail. Many are struggling to return to some semblance of a normal life.**

They have been separated from their families for years. They have had their rights stripped from them. They can't vote. They can't own a firearm.

Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions.

_And they were hunted down in a political persecution that denied them their constitutional rights. _

So what comes next for J6ers?

They can't own a firearm. Not only are these men and women patriots, but they come from all walks of life -- law enforcement, veterans, white-collar professionals, blue-collar workers, and all races and religions. We want them to know that they are not forgotten. This begins by providing housing and vehicles, counseling, and confidential peer support; the tools needed for healing and reintegration. The J6ers are our neighbors. They are sons and daughters, brothers and sisters, mothers and fathers. It is up to us to ensure that they have the resources needed to rebuild their lives and reclaim their dignity. subject: Your zip code shouldn't determine your future
body:

I grew up in Peoria, Illinois.
It's not a coastal city or a tech hub. It's not the kind of place that shows up in conversations about the economy of the future. Just a midwestern town where working families built good lives — and where too many of those families today are watching the opportunities their parents had disappear without anything replacing them.
That's not a Peoria problem – that's an American problem.
Right now, where you live — your zip code — plays too large a role in determining what kind of future you can build. If you're in the right city, near the right industries, with access to the right schools and training programs, the 21st century economy has a place for you. If you're not — if you're in a small town, an urban area, a rural community, a neighborhood that the market has decided isn't worth investing in — you're on your own.
That is not acceptable. And it is not inevitable.
That's why I founded Equal Opportunity Now, to elect real leaders who will work to make sure EVERY American has a shot at the American Dream. Click here to rush a donation, then keep reading! [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]
Your zip code should not determine whether you have access to in-demand jobs that pay good wages and provide real security for your family. It should not determine whether you can learn the skills the modern economy actually needs. It should not determine whether your community gets to participate in the growth and innovation that is reshaping our world.
We need to invest in career and technical education, in apprenticeships, in the kinds of training programs that meet people where they are and give them a real path forward. We need to bring business development to every part of this country — not just the coasts, not just the cities — and make sure that when those investments come, the people who already live there are the ones who benefit.
This is core to what Equal Opportunity Now is fighting for. Because expanding opportunity doesn't just mean tearing down barriers. It means building something in their place.
Will you chip in $5 or $10 today to help us elect leaders who will fight to make sure every American — regardless of their zip code — has a real shot at the future? [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/eon-email]

Let's make sure it doesn't.

subject: I stopped Trump’s illegal anti-science scheme
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Lofgren for Congress
body:

Hi Peter, it's Zoe.

I have good news: the Trump administration just backed off an illegal scheme to rip apart one of our most important ocean monitoring systems.
Here's what happened:

The National Science Foundation quietly moved to dismantle the Ocean Observatories Initiative – a network of instruments on the ocean floor that scientists, fishermen, and coastal communities rely on to track everything from tsunamis to changing ocean conditions.

They didn't ask Congress. They didn't ask scientists. They just started pulling research buoys off the Pacific Northwest coast.

It was reckless, and it was illegal.

So I did what I always do when this administration tries to govern by chaos: I pushed back, hard, alongside my Democratic colleagues.

And we won. Critical research will continue in the Pacific Northwest and help protect our planet for years to come.

Peter, this is a win. But I'm not quite celebrating yet, because:

[1] We still don't know how much damage they've already done. Instruments are missing from the ocean floor right now.

[2] The Trump administration hasn't committed to replacing what they destroyed, or to stop acting until real scientists are back in the room.

[3] This is exactly the kind of reactionary, lawless governing Trump's agencies do every single day when nobody's watching.

As the Ranking Member of the Science, Space, and Technology Committee, I'm not going anywhere. My oversight team will keep pressing NSF until every instrument is replaced and every decision runs through legitimate scientific review, not political panic.

But I can only keep doing this work if I win re-election in November. Peter, will you chip in $5, $25, or whatever you can to help me keep holding this administration accountable? >> [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/e-zoe-lofgren-q32026?refcode=EM_ALL_ZOL_FR_1_2026-07-08_SCI_ZOL_ES-53414&amount=25]

name: Scott Wiener
subject: 7 years of hard work.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Scott WIENER FOR CONGRESS
body:
| |

Peter -

**After 7 years of hard work, my landmark housing bill has officially taken effect in California, clearing the way to build as many as 1.5 million new homes near public transit.**

That’s a big deal.

And it comes on the heels of last year’s historic reforms, which cut through red tape and made it easier to build affordable housing in California.

None of this was easy. The status quo fought me every step of the way. But we won because I refused to accept that California’s housing crisis is somehow inevitable.

Last week, _The New York Times_ wrote about Andy's work to elect Democrats across the country in 2026, and we wanted to make sure you saw it:

[_**Read the NYT article and learn more about the work Andy is doing to elect good leaders this fall >>>**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/134901404/632519178/-1673894281?refcode=ITT_ATA_EM_FR_NYT_260708_T1_1&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTAzNjMiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNjkwMjFjYzUtMjA3Yi1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=4cy7_g3bz0ujo92pjoPpLlnpih8FoM_Lk_cRMIeXKFw=&emci=e2c305ba-7c79-f111-ac9c-000d3a14b6d6&emdi=69021cc5-207b-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=17458827)

# Kevin in the Community
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | | **Door Knocking in East Central for Yes for Buses!** Saturday, June 20th was the yes for buses canvassing kick-off where I had the chance to help spread the word about the importance of continued public transit funding. I endorse Prop 1, which does not increase taxes, as it allows the Spokane Transit Authority to maintain service levels and to continue to qualify for necessary grants. Public transit is one of the many great things about Spokane, so make sure to vote YES for buses on August 4!
---
| | | | | | | | | | | |

**Endorsed by the Environment and Climate Caucus of the WA State Democrats** I am incredibly excited to be the only District 5 candidate endorsed by the State Democratic Party’s Environment and Climate Council. Our climate and public lands are in crisis, and we need representatives in Congress who are going to fight to reverse climate change and protect public lands. This endorsement is a recognition of my commitment to these goals and the years that I have already devoted to

| | Friend,

I have good news!

After years of pushing for stronger oversight and accountability in King County, the County Council has approved my legislation to create a new Inspector General Division to help fight fraud, waste, and abuse.

**The waste and misuse of public dollars is not a hypothetical problem, and taxpayers deserve better. **[Read about the legislation in the Seattle Times here.](https://us.list-manage.com/FOfDpeWmy0H?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166) They deserve to know that their hard-earned dollars are being protected. When public dollars are wasted, misused, or abused, government has a responsibility to investigate, recover misspent funds, and require meaningful consequences.

**That is why I was proud to co-sponsor and help author this legislation.**

The new Inspector General Division will give King County the teeth it needs to uncover improper spending, conduct rigorous oversight, and recover misspent funds.
[](https://us.list-manage.com/3pb81Kqm6x4?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166) **_" Taxpayers have had enough. They deserve a government that delivers real accountability and justice for financial wrongdoing."_**
**\- Councilmember Reagan Dunn**
_**This is a real win for accountability. But there is much more work to do. [Support my efforts here!](https://us.list-manage.com/EV5riKGfWJG?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)**_

With affordability a top concern, _**_I will never stop fighting_** _to root out waste, demand accountability, and ensure taxpayer dollars are spent efficiently.

If you are able, I would be grateful for your support as I continue this work.**A[contribution of $35, $50, $75, or whatever you able](https://us.list-manage.com/pySOBKR9AhR?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166) helps me continue demanding accountability and protecting taxpayer dollars.** **\----------------------
[DONATE NOW](https://us.list-manage.com/16E2vdMvhwp?e=77eef70c61&c2id=352d4c3b964128868a59384c192ed166)
\----------------------** Friend, I can't thank you enough for standing with me and making this work possible!

Reagan Dunn

Peter,

We have our work cut out for us, though. Republicans are seeing our campaign grow by the day, they’re reading the headlines and they know we have what it takes to flip this seat.
That’s why their super PACs are pouring nearly $100 million so far into this race to halt our momentum – and experts predict this will be the most expensive Senate race in history.

body:
NY-07 is one step closer to sending a fearless, working class fighter to Congress.
# [](https://act.leaderswedeserve.com/go/852?refcode=em20260708-1&t=1&akid=3697%2E587540%2EHA6O4W)
New York is entering a new era, Peter.
And last month, the people of Brooklyn and Queens chose their next fighter. **Claire Valdez has officially won her primary in NY-07!** 🎉
This is a monumental win for working New Yorkers. Claire ran for Congress because she believes deeply in the people who make our city run, and in our collective power to build a future that actually works for us. She’s bringing a bold, unapologetic vision for working people, and I know that in Washington, she’ll fight for it without flinching.
Before she ever ran for office, Claire was a fierce labor organizer who went toe-to-toe with management. That kind of fire and conviction can’t be bought. It’s earned, one picket line, one bargaining table, and one community at a time.
That’s who Claire is. And it’s why she won this race the _right_ way: powered entirely by working people, refusing every single dime of real estate, fossil fuel, and AIPAC money. The only people she’s accountable to are the people of her district.
**This is why I keep saying that the movement of young people, immigrants, and workers who put me in the Mayor’s office was never just about one person. It’s about whether working people have the power to shape the future they deserve. One grounded in dignity and in a politics that delivers.**
Claire’s win is proof that the answer is a resounding **_yes._** Here in New York, and everywhere else this movement is taking root.

Trump Moves to Cut Off Spain
President Trump opened the second day of the NATO summit in Ankara by ordering the U.S. to [cut off trade](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2unDAQQOGngc7IO2B-Chdp6DZtSjR4hsWKwRZj4uzbX21xX-D2R19x_jyXJ_rgz9dvPNh6kYUiLRiduP0--JI9Forl9Ofh3e4X0NArPSg9LumKktjlBWqyBh7jNtZsH8PYGtNNpq13u209jMhk-nbojHHdsOp17aZHDxNAz7W3H1APeoTWGAMN4jptZqNxaqetJ6w6fSfCzI0_xROLizGlGHz2Tpp4vepg95yTVO2vCuYK5lJKs8X_JxdpXDwqmL_zCuZ83UdSxAeeJIpPUvlCYvWX3-oWhSG8lcMQRBWUzKQc3sL1ZSkVH4KXfqg6_TrQhw9e5x8v-2fhKwAA___HkoDD) with Spain, the only alliance member refusing NATO's 5% defense-spending target. He branded Madrid a ["terrible partner"](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LGupSAQgOGnwQ7DHQ-KhcU2dnfbLc0Ic46zQSAwrq-_8RXuC_x_8v353r6RI6fPbzxp4da2kMOG2Td_XCfVduQ75DtxOtkfvIGBUZtJG7eVmlshLxt0YbHw5d6uo-VrcoO1r9kO3bEMIxK-dmen3QQK4z6AMTBbN0x72MPe8fIEzWQcDNZa6BH3-W3fwc3D_B4Dqpe5SkChnlPjQM3nXEqOLOxbn-uni8shUpoafilYFaz3ffc3toPTR3ISPqn1Pp8K1kR3U7A-RwXr3ysqWJ2CNeSEMWip11m0HJVQKDXtL9FSMZBuBTlpj_GB0kK18h5JF6ySqOqEkhWsXV1CuTlGbuOkXuZzIsdn3cmPYf8t8D8AAP__0LmNyQ) that "doesn't participate" and "doesn't pay," directing Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent to halt commerce immediately. Trump also faulted Spain for denying U.S. forces its air bases during operations against Iran. Dismissing the country as a ["wasted cause,"](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2ypiAQheHVYKaF_PhpQDCJ2Z10Qqsv3UpXKVCCwyx_yi3c_JwneP98bV_AJ8fjN1zkuJQNE26QfPHhueguITVMLXK82AfelFRTLz-9nLd8p5LJ10116Kwa533uyI2fWVtrFqu74BAXDdNuRgSpdiRtPWoko7_NJP2oO3YvKD9yVtpaqwaA72W3O86LXvYJQRj5ZIRKA8fCSMWnlHM6ubIvQ7qP7nSh1lyE_iXUKtTaWhsalMDxqCnSP7g40j34dAm1Rmrl3QSu1If0FBJqNZOezWiFWuv9XLmvNyD1JQPHPkJNPT70vrrbYW58nlymjzDyuIDPF-7qj8v9dep_AAAA__9y7II3) he predicted Spanish officials would come "running back." Prime Minister Pedro Sanchez's office shrugged off the threat as business as usual. ★★★
McConnell Health Questions Mount
Speculation over Sen. Mitch McConnell intensified as the 84-year-old entered a fourth week hospitalized after a June 14 medical emergency. Kentucky Gov. Andy Beshear formally [requested an update](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2ynSAUxfGnwQ6Hg6JYUKSxu2lTOvsAys7lw7jxMnn7jMkbpF_z_82sHx_bB2DEfHyH5A0Sba64DYolG-7kLwqludIy5oQ24CaFnLiYudDbeRU6va2b7JxR8qV33XnzmvWg1LiooQtGWNDglmmQg1Vvq8Avr_eodzHDrCxAh-YJilloOSilZA_wXna1O70Myz45YKO4TwfV95gJnSdbynmWiBUt9eU6umhCrSex4RuTK5Nra61vQAHzUUuumDz1tiQm1-wbMbk-IpPrzzsyuWom10-f620_f_OjfPkrl4tf_tftqRL_Z_OE1QaerC05-xiJBw-xBv53hSU_2e4y7mwYI9I0s1EcCTA-clf_-9cvI_8EAAD__9bSjlM) on the senator's condition, citing constituents' growing concern. McConnell's office has [disclosed no details](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LFutDAQBOCnMR3IGIxx4eJv6O5vU6LFNsdKxmuxvpySp48o8gJpRlPNJ83HY30AJszP_3BGh8xroLACefbH64wXH_QO9M6YT_QHrkqqqZWmlfNaLuISfV1VE5xW_bzPTXS9mQetR6uH5nBbb9U-bAYi9NaaaRxA2dHGOEo9mc026O5BaeSsBq216gA2u-s9zHaw-xRAjPJVAtTYYWYMkT1RKZSwoueOrmeT3FFrYTH8E2oRagmA6ctDSvHqPJ1CLTch1CLNb5zeU84xpZYr7Hu8uGVMMdf2IC5YIeE3VKTcesoB7ybU0lwulDemhDwZMcrnCZhuoql_Pu7TqZ8AAAD__3sVgMU), repeating only that he "continues to improve" while working with staff during the recess. Pushing back on online rumors, Majority Leader John Thune and Whip John Barrasso said phone calls left them finding McConnell ["fully engaged."](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DGy2zoMQNHVUB01NCTaVKHiN-reb1NqYBI2kVAER6CjLD_ztpAN3LlzfnztX8iF6_t_PGhl1T1J2lGixvw56NQsV5Krcj04Zt7Bwd26h3Vhb6doo9h3GNLq4RZeYaD19giT9_PipyGv0wzTMgMFwoQTEszeYUjzDejmvKOB1--ge7gAk_ceRsTn8vKvFJZped0Tmtl9WsJOI1flRBpFWpPCnaOOcr6Hsubem5rpPwObge26rvFCzVzfXSr9wYMrnWOUw8BW6VIDm1LFTga2-T4tLgQDW5dmT2qfZ-GIVa02-UW2ZalkI5ZiD-4x2yNGqZVKsVfmQparzaKNOxb7U3K1TzxPVBUD23CuqV1cCuv9YWb3PpDL98jQ_1n69wp_AwAA__8lFJPu) His absence strains a narrow GOP majority as the Senate returns July 13. ★★★
OpenAI Model Cleared for Release
OpenAI announced its most advanced series, GPT-5.6, will get a full [public rollout](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLHOpCAURp8GOwwDglpQbGM3225p7sBVboJABMfdt9_4Cn_5Fd85yfnzXt9AkdL-Gw60VOvqs18hu-rCdeBZQ759vhOlg1ygVQppuBi5mNZy5lrQtVV23mr5mrapQ_saJ6X1MGvVBesUGOnNNCBq5QGdEEYJBDcaFJ9568g-QDGKSSqttewBPvOmNz_Nat6MBzaIq3ho2FOq5LG6nEvJkRq52udz76INrZXK1C8mFyaX-777G2qgtLec8C8clPDsXT6YXJ6n-8fk0tCFlGPenzGYQUgxM7nkggmIR2hYG__iWSkn7gK0vTRerk8kx9t5HYUXuCoyuXSn9eWmGKmakQ1iP4Dio-vaj3t-rfwfAAD__411izk) Thursday, ending weeks of federal limits under President Trump's new AI framework. Trump's June executive order set up a voluntary process inviting frontier labs to submit powerful models for [government review](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D1yhCAUAODTaIeDuCAWFGnsNm1KB-G5vgl_48OQ42f2CrnAV3xfz-1pMWB6fdoIBok2n_1msyN33hEuOnPzuSVMEd2Jm-BCMT4zrrdyZSrg6iZ6b6QY9aF7MOOsJykfi5z600wA-6hh8VIfbtHC6XmXs5NKj0pwpXo0b5DPXItJSikGa_flkIfXy7Qcytvuwe_ibYUBE6EHcjmXkgNWdDTk69UHc9ZaqJs-OrF2Ym2tDUf-TdBocDl2YiWHkBx0Yq3XHQsrdyW2X_YbiOUCySKxBA2oMossZg-hv4wvDUNAUnP34K9oMby5vv476ceIvwAAAP__7fN7uA) before release. The administration had earlier pressed OpenAI to restrict access to vetted partners over [cybersecurity concerns](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2OpDAUBODTQAain_8DB5uQ9aYbIrf9jJ9ksIXd25rbj5gjTFil0hfUv-f2dJTp3P-6Ay21toUSNld88-l94NVS-YTyOek8yCfaYAE5LWpa9Fav0ir6vsEYrICHjnpE-1CaCcGNYGOymkPkhgUpDRecoXpF9F5HJQC052Yke4OLWjQwIQTMzr1MFDFow0yUwQ18edfgOs50NgrYfCm1lkydfJvLtY_Zpt5rG9ifAdYB1p4wUc6zL8cA6z31X3eNPp0ll_0OwggtuZpKxdPRdGFG17BNe-1CTv16H3WAdbxsqB_KmZpUA1_2w9GPO_ZfP_XfwncAAAD__0Thezk). Rival Anthropic faced similar treatment last month when Commerce restricted its Mythos and Fable models before lifting the order July 1. A White House official insisted no clearance is required and release timing rests with the companies.
Michigan's socialist showdown

The Aug. 4 Democratic Senate primary has become a proxy war between the party's warring wings. Bernie Sanders-backed Abdul El-Sayed is the [emerging front-runner](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0D2OpDAQxfHTQGZE27gNAcEmZLPphqiwCyjJX3J52tu3X_UeYS7w03v_P1_7F5CneP2GgCsx7y65HZJle38HLHyn5lKLFAPZm3Y5yqcYjRjnPZfEGW3dZe9WLR_zOfe4PsystJ4Wrfp7neSiJkR7noeZD43mgdNhwSx2eThlxp7WDziacZZKay0HgGM59enmRS3n00E3jd_ZQcWBIpNDtinlnDxVsjykcvV-vWvN3Klfndw6ubXWhgZ8U7xqivgXAkUsg02hk1vExp3cpqcys1ad3P6_uiAKxggVRS4UoLyFw5Bsgcoil3QVZKYXskCucHjiO2CsAr1geKMTN3h8C674wvjx-7K63Mh74qfppvEKQP4zoa8_bvxa5b8AAAD__wt2k1w) over Schumer-favorite Rep. Haley Stevens, and AOC's endorsement of El-Sayed has turned the contest into a referendum on Democratic leadership itself.

North Carolina drifts left

With Sen. Thom Tillis retiring, former Democratic Gov. Roy Cooper holds a mid-single-digit [polling edge](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLGupiAUhJ8GOw0eQLGg2IbubrulORdQT4JAgPubffuNr7DlNN_MfH--9i-kSOn8jXcw1Nrus98xu-aunzvUduXH5ydRusldtAOHZeTryPVeam4luL7D4I2CWR96CGZetVBKbkoMl5mV1ErgoqXY-IxiO7gT34uTs9SznN1A5gXylWsQSimYEL-3Qx1eb2I7Fo9M8p_isYeJUiMfmsu5lBypk2tTrucQzdV7aUz8YmAZ2Od5phowuhiwlhzfc5PLNwP7psbAtpCwBwb2DClUjAzsO4OBTbn2a3RYc6SEDOxbF-r4aeNzYY_h71CNLw_FSG1ZmeTnjRRf_tD_W9_HwL8AAAD__3g7gwQ) over Trump-backed former RNC Chairman Michael Whatley. The open seat is Democrats' likeliest flip target; losing it would all but end their path to a Senate majority.

★★★
A Kentucky seat in play?

McConnell's hospitalization has revived questions about a possible vacancy. Under a 2024 law, Democratic Gov. Andy Beshear could only [call a special election](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2ynSAUxfGnwQ6Hg6JYUKSxu2lTOvsAys7lw7jxMnn7jMkbpF_z_82sHx_bB2DEfHyH5A0Sba64DYolG-7kLwqludIy5oQ24CaFnLiYudDbeRU6va2b7JxR8qV33XnzmvWg1LiooQtGWNDglmmQg1Vvq8Avr_eodzHDrCxAh-YJilloOSilZA_wXna1O70Myz45YKO4TwfV95gJnSdbynmWiBUt9eU6umhCrSex4RuTK5Nra61vQAHzUUuumDz1tiQm1-wbMbk-IpPrzzsyuWom10-f620_f_OjfPkrl4tf_tftqRL_Z_OE1QaerC05-xiJBw-xBv53hSU_2e4y7mwYI9I0s1EcCTA-clf_-9cvI_8EAAD__9bSjlM), not appoint a replacement, injecting fresh uncertainty into an already narrow GOP majority.

SAVE Act meets NDAA
Conservatives are pressing Speaker Mike Johnson's gambit to attach the SAVE America Act to the must-pass defense bill, arguing the [Supreme Court's ruling](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0L2OtCAUxvGrgU6DB_mwoHgbu3nbLc1ZQD0JChFmzN79ZjbZG9jmKX9P8v94LA-kROf2H4_oqNYl5LBg9tXvzyNedc93yPdJ50F-pwUE6E6YTtilXLmW6NsCPDgFg10tj24wVio1Tkry3UVtVh8QRw168FNcp4gCtbVSG2W15OTeoDDCglRKQY_4Oa1qDXaS06oDslE8S8AWezorhVh9zqXkRI187fO18eT21kpl8h-DmcF833cfkNJXpe3E1Pt8MJjfNwxmYX6n4it2eMSLPHboW7flwmDmlwvlppSoasNGsR1IPwZvf67zcvAdAAD__0IHdck) permitting late-arriving mail-in ballots makes proof-of-citizenship voting rules urgent before November. ★★★
Florida targets media blacklists

Gov. Ron DeSantis signed a budget provision barring state agencies from hiring ad firms that use "misinformation" ratings from outfits like [NewsGuard](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0DFuhDAQheHTmA5kDMZQuEhDt2lTosFjwygGI8YbK7ePNlIukOaV35P-j8fyAIp0bu9weEvMCyZcIDl2-_PwN--pYConnQe5nRYl1VBLU8txue7El3d5URVardoxjJW3rRk7rftJd9Vu5eA1BmPW4FVop1Z7D3oY1r4dJqP9WJF9gdLIUXVaa9UArFPQAcepm8KAIHr5vBCyb-hkQs8upetKkTI5btK9VdHuOV8sujehZqHmUkqDQPGbaTshNi4dQs2vG6Fmaf4mxHQTQn14JKjXCO4zEmeuT194e8KNQs3VbfEqFCPxYEQvtwPoV6zyv1t9WfUTAAD__zHRe6g) to steer dollars away from outlets. Backers call it a shield for conservative media against AI-driven blacklisting.

AI order gates model releases

Trump's June executive order created a voluntary framework that allows federal agencies to [review frontier models](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyckLHOpCAURp8GOwwDglpQbGM3225p7sBVboJABMfdt9_4Cn_5Fd85yfnzXt9AkdL-Gw60VOvqs18hu-rCdeBZQ759vhOlg1ygVQppuBi5mNZy5lrQtVV23mr5mrapQ_saJ6X1MGvVBesUGOnNNCBq5QGdEEYJBDcaFJ9568g-QDGKSSqttewBPvOmNz_Nat6MBzaIq3ho2FOq5LG6nEvJkRq52udz76INrZXK1C8mFyaX-777G2qgtLec8C8clPDsXT6YXJ6n-8fk0tCFlGPenzGYQUgxM7nkggmIR2hYG__iWSkn7gK0vTRerk8kx9t5HYUXuCoyuXSn9eWmGKmakQ1iP4Dio-vaj3t-rfwfAAD__411izk) before public release. Supporters cite cybersecurity concerns; critics warn that Washington now holds a kill switch over private AI, potentially ceding ground to China's open-source rivals.

1. **Spain blinked, and Trump knows it**
Madrid's shrug masks real exposure: Spanish bonds and the IBEX slid on the [trade threat](https://email.update.insidescooppolitics.org/c/eJyc0LGupSAQgOGnwQ7DHQ-KhcU2dnfbLc0Ic46zQSAwrq-_8RXuC_x_8v353r6RI6fPbzxp4da2kMOG2Td_XCfVduQ75DtxOtkfvIGBUZtJG7eVmlshLxt0YbHw5d6uo-VrcoO1r9kO3bEMIxK-dmen3QQK4z6AMTBbN0x72MPe8fIEzWQcDNZa6BH3-W3fwc3D_B4Dqpe5SkChnlPjQM3nXEqOLOxbn-uni8shUpoafilYFaz3ffc3toPTR3ISPqn1Pp8K1kR3U7A-RwXr3ysqWJ2CNeSEMWip11m0HJVQKDXtL9FSMZBuBTlpj_GB0kK18h5JF6ySqOqEkhWsXV1CuTlGbuOkXuZzIsdn3cmPYf8t8D8AAP__0LmNyQ).
